articles.title: Shae Cruyff, nieto de Johan, convocado con Estados Unidos
articles.standfirst: El legado del exjugador neerlandés continúa: es internacional sub 18
articles.summary: El legado del exjugador neerlandés continúa: es internacional sub 18
articles.body: El apellido Cruyff sigue vinculado al mundo del fútbol. El legado del mítico exjugador y exentrenador, fallecido en 2016, continúa. Tras la trayectoria de su hijo, Jordi, ahora es su nieto Shea quien da pasos importantes en el balompié: ha sido convocado por la selección sub18 de Estados Unidos. Shea Cruyff-Beane, el hijo menor de Chantal Cruyff, fue citado en las últimas horas por el combinado americano, que disputará dos encuentros. El nieto de Johan, que juega de centrocampista, milita en las categorías inferiores del Nàstic de Tarragona. Shea posee tres nacionalidades: la de España (donde nació), Países Bajos (procedencia de su familia materna) y Estados Unidos (origen de su padre). Ahora ha sido citado por la sub 18 americana, pero aún podría variar su equipo nacional en el futuro. El fútbol ha acompañado siempre a Shea, ya que no sólo es nieto y sobrino de profesionales de este deporte sino que su padre, Todd Beane, militó en el Dartmouth College, en la primera división de la NCAA, y llegó a jugar como profesional en su país. La selección sub 18 de Estados Unidos se medirá a Portugal y Noruega en el país luso.

articles.title: El Barça de Flick sabe sufrir
articles.standfirst: El bloque culé suma cuatro remontadas este curso y con el técnico germano, 23
articles.summary: El bloque culé suma cuatro remontadas este curso y con el técnico germano, 23
articles.body: El Barcelona sabe sufrir. Es un equipo acostumbrado a divertirse y a deleitar a los aficionados del fútbol, pero también sabe arremangarse y reconducir los partidos cuando su arranque no resulta todo lo exitoso que tenía planeado. El Barcelona ha protagonizado cuatro remontadas ya esta temporada, tres de ellas en LaLiga, no se rindió y superó el marcador adverso contra el Rayo, el Sevilla y el Atlético, y una en la Champions League: le dio la vuelta al marcador en el cruce continental contra el Galatasaray. El pasado fin de semana, el Barça de Flick consiguió, por tercera temporada consecutiva, remontar un partido en el Riyadh Air Metropolitano para llevarse los tres puntos. "En la primera parte, estábamos muy lejos del rival, pero en la segunda lo corregimos y lo hicimos mucho mejor en ese aspecto", reconoció Flick tras el encuentro contra los de Simeone, aportando una de las claves de la remontada. El conjunto culé, además, es el segundo equipo de las cinco grandes ligas europeas que muestra una mayor capacidad de reacción en competición doméstica. Solo el Inter de Milán, con cuatro remontadas, supera a los azulgranas. El Barça comparte la segunda posición con el Racing de Santander, también con tres remontadas en la LaLiga. Desde que Hansi Flick accediera al banquillo del conjunto catalán, en verano de 2024, el conjunto azulgrana ha protagonizado 23 remontadas en 133 encuentros. Firmó 9 en la campaña 24-25, 10 en la pasada, la 25-26, y esta ya suma cuatro. El técnico culé ha enseñado a sus hombres a no rendirse y a trabajar hasta enmendar, en muchos casos, los errores y resultados adversos. El germano está a una de Pep Guardiola, que consiguió 24 en 249 partidos, y a cinco de Johan Cruyff, que logró 28 en 430.

articles.title: España quiere aprovecharse del ciclón Fermín
articles.standfirst: Bigoleador en el Metropolitano, ocho dianas en lo que va de temporada y a la caza de estrenarse con España
articles.summary: Bigoleador en el Metropolitano, ocho dianas en lo que va de temporada y a la caza de estrenarse con España
articles.body: Fermín defendió el liderato del Barcelona con dos goles marca de la casa en el Metropolitano. Dos tantos marca de la casa, de centrocampista llegador. Su cuenta esta temporada se eleva a ocho. La pasada la cerró también con ocho. El barcelonista se suma a la selección en un gran momento de forma, extendido desde que arrancó la temporada. Fermín forma parte del tridente que tiene líder al Barça en la Liga y muy bien situado en la Champions para entrar entre los ocho mejores. A sus ocho goles suma siete asistencias. A su lado, Raphinha (19/3) y Lamine Yamal (13/12). Ese poder goleador de Fermín busca encontrar su espacio en la selección. Después de diez partidos y 312 minutos, el andaluz aún no ha encontrado las redes rivales. La verdad es que la continuidad no ha aparecido en su camino como internacional, con las lesiones como principales responsables. De la Fuente llegó a la selección para la Eurocopa de 2024. Debutó en el amistoso ante Andorra en Badajoz (5-0) y su papel en el campo durante la Euro se limitó a 28 minutos ante Albania, en el tercer partido y con España ya clasificada y primera de grupo. De allí se fue a los Juegos. En París, Fermín fue clave para el oro español: seis goles, dos de ellos en la final, una asistencia... Él y Baena vivieron un verano espectacular. Nadie antes había sido campeón de Europa y olímpico a la vez con minutos en las dos competiciones. El francés Albert Rust lo fue en 1984, pero el portero de Mulhouse no jugó ningún minuto en la Eurocopa. Después llegaron las lesiones. Desde la final de la Euro hasta la Final Four de 2025 no hubo noticias de Fermín en la selección. Entre lesiones e irregularidad, no recuperó su sitio hasta la Final Four, en la que no jugó un solo minuto. Al Mundial llegaba Fermín con la flecha hacia arriba, como un elemento vital para De la Fuente a la hora de cambiar partidos y sumar goles. Pero en la penúltima jornada de Liga, a una semana de la lista y sin nada en juego, Fermín se fracturó el quinto metatarsiano del pie derecho. Lo que iba a ser su primer Mundial pasó a ser un quirófano y ver a España ser campeona por la tele Todo eso queda en el recuerdo de un jugador de solo 23 años. Fermín vuelve a ser ese centrocampista que tanto valoran los entrenadores, el que es capaz de acabar la temporada con diez o más goles. Esa frontera, con menos de un tercio de campaña consumido, la tiene a solo dos tantos. En Praga, y en un contexto sin Dani Olmo en el equipo, Fermín afronta su undécimo partido con España. Le esperan aún las sensaciones de celebrar su primer gol con España. En el banquillo rival estará Santi Denia, el entrenador con el que se abrazó y celebró el oro de París.

articles.title: La 'auctoritas' de Mourinho
articles.summary: Una opinión de Manuel Julía
articles.body: La autoridad más sólida que he visto en mi vida fue la de mi profesor de filosofía. Era un tipo callado, de cabello gris y mirada de sabio astuto, esa que, dicen, tenía Sócrates. Le lanzábamos las más difíciles preguntas y nos respondía con las más sencillas respuestas. Era muy cincuentón y le gustaba hablarnos de su experiencia de las cosas más que de su conocimiento de ellas. Había perdido, por tanto, la soberbia del saber. Me recuerda a Mourinho en las ruedas de prensa o en las entrevistas. Ha perdido gestos a cambio de palabras medidas y astutas. Sé que en el vestuario ha conseguido esa auctoritas que no viene del poder, sino del convencimiento. En el paraninfo de la Universidad de Salamanca, hace muchísimo tiempo, dijo Unamuno a un auditorio lleno de soldados vencedores que la mayor victoria es la de persuadir. Lo cuenta Alejandro Amenábar. Ahí está ese poder maravilloso que no emana de la jerarquía, sino de la capacidad de unir voluntades en un propósito aceptado. El vestuario del Madrid se tragó a varios entrenadores por tenerlos controlados. Llegó Mou y llegó un general dialogante. Llegó Mou y llegó la aceptación por el convencimiento, por la admiración y la certeza de que siguiendo la estela del jefe se llega a un destino bueno. Todos reman en la misma dirección, si saben dónde van, y además están de acuerdo. Las ansiadas lluvias llegan. El cielo se comprime en una cúpula de sombras blancas. A veces se desbordan ríos. Cambio climático, inestabilidad... El frío amaga, pero se esconde detrás de las cortinas del paisaje. En mi lugar, la tierra, casi siempre gris o marrón, está cogiendo un verdor de Asturias o de Escocia. Veo al seleccionador llegar adonde quizá haya más frío y lluvia. Los lamentos por la ausencia de Lamine Yamal le persiguen. Dicen que no quiere molestar al Barça. No lo creo. Confío en él. Pero los aficionados se quejan. Muchos hicieron el viaje por verle. Las estrellas son la luz, sí, pero los equipos son la lumbre, sin la cual todo sería oscuridad. En cualquier otro país tener una selección como la nuestra sería un orgullo absoluto. Pero aquí, acostumbrados a la polarización, trasladamos todas nuestras disputas diarias a la selección y hasta escucho absurdos debates de apropiación indebida. Este país nuestro, España con todas sus sílabas, realiza gestas deportivas al alcance de pocos y es campeón mundial en tantas disciplinas que da vergüenza decirlo. ¡Saquemos el pecho de una vez! Sin peros, sin terruños, sin ideologías excluyentes, sin egoísmos, sin soberbias de clubes, sin que vaya contra nadie, sin extraños debates en los que se habla de todo menos de fútbol.

articles.title: El 'Barrylete cósmico' que acecha a Haaland: "Me gusta demostrar a los críticos que se equivocan"
articles.standfirst: El ex del Villarreal, ahora en el Everton, acumula 10 goles ya este curso, seis en Premier
articles.summary: El ex del Villarreal, ahora en el Everton, acumula 10 goles ya este curso, seis en Premier
articles.body: Barry ya no está Thierno. El ex del Villarreal, traspasado al Everton en 2025 a cambio de 30 millones de euros, se ha erigido en el goleador del momento en la Premier League. Sólo Erling Haaland (9) y Alexander Isak (7) superan las seis dianas del '9' del Everton en la lucha por la 'Bota de Oro' de la Premier League. Sin embargo, el francés, internacional sub 21, llega lanzado. Los cuatro goles y las dos asistencias que acumula en los últimos tres partidos de Liga han aupado al equipo que dirige David Moyes a la sexta plaza. Atrás quedan las críticas que recibió después de no conseguir anotar su primer gol en Premier hasta la jornada 15 y cerrar el curso con ocho goles. "Todos los días mi familia me envía capturas de gente en redes diciendo que soy el peor delantero, pero a mí las críticas no me importan. Me gusta demostrar que se equivocan quienes tienen una idea errónea de mí", reconocía allá por el mes de enero. Su progresión desde que en 2022 recalara en el Beveren procedente del filial del Sochaux. Un año después -marcó 20 goles en 33 partidos- fichó por el Basilea y sólo otro años más tarde -anotó 20 tantos en 41 encuentros- aterrizó en El Madrigal previo pago de 13,5 millones de euros. A las órdenes de Marcelino García Toral también fue de menos a más, hasta registrar 11 goles y cuatro asistencias en los 35 partidos que disputó en su primer curso en LaLiga. "Era un chico atlético, con unas capacidades físicas que impresionaban, pero que nunca había estado en la cantera de un equipo grande y eso se notaba en aspectos como la metodología, la comprensión del juego o la toma de decisiones", recuerda Sergio García, hijo y ayudante de Marcelino, a MARCA. Un físico privilegiado que le viene de familia: su madre fue atleta de 800 metros y su padre fue internacional por Guinea en baloncesto. Detrás, eso sí, hay mucho trabajo en la sombra: "Siempre quería entrenar más para mejorar: hacía sesiones individuales, trabajaba las finalizaciones con ambas piernas y el remate de cabeza. Es cierto que en ocasiones le costaba entender cómo sacar partido a todas sus virtudes y expresarlas en el campo. También llamaba la atención su generosidad para hacer movimientos que favorecían a sus compañeros y generaban espacios, incluso cuando eso le alejaba a él de hacer gol", insiste Sergio García. En Villarreal también duró sólo un año. “Ha sido una aventura loca que nos ha llevado a clasificarnos para la Champions League”, se podía leer en su despedida. Le costó adaptarse a la Premier. "Aquí el juego es más físico. Soy alto, pero no corpulento, así que necesito trabajar mi cuerpo para saber cómo usarlo para proteger el balón", reconocía. Esta vez, comenzó el curso con la lección aprendida. "Esta temporada tiene que ser la mía. Me he esforzado mucho este verano para conseguirlo, así que estoy muy contento de haber marcado mi primer hat-trick con el Everton", vaticinó tras Barry, que suma cuatro goles más en Copa de la Liga, tras derrotar al Preston NE (0-4). Diez goles en total. Sólo Haaland (14) ha marcado más en Inglaterra contando todas las competiciones. “Estoy muy contento porque soy fan de Haaland. Veo muchos vídeos suyos e intento imitar lo que hace. Intentaré pelear hasta el final para conseguir el 'Pichichi", advierte Barry. "Es cierto que la temporada pasada falló bastantes ocasiones, pero se está convirtiendo en una pieza importante para nosotros. ¡No sé si Haaland estará preocupado por que lo alcance ahora! No veo a muchos delanteros jóvenes marcando tantos goles en la Premier League", aseguraba David Moyes. No son sólo los goles. El ex del Villarreal es el jugador de la Premier que más duelos aéreos gana (45), el segundo que más dispara, tanto en total (36) como a puerta (15) y el tercero que más 'sprints' realiza (145). Aún así, quiere más. "Para un goleador lo más importante es tener ocasiones para marcar. La temporada pasada creo que estuvo 12 partidos sin marcar, así que estoy contento mi momento actual. Ahora sólo necesito concentrarme en mejorar mi finalización", señala. El trabajo en la sombra está dando sus frutos: "He trabajado un montón desde la pretemporada con Leighton Baines para dar lo mejor de mí cada fin de semana. Las cosas ahora van mejor. Los aficionados me conocen más y estoy feliz". David Moyes, por su parte, se vanagloria del negocio que hizo el Everton: "Tiene una gran ética de trabajo. Creo que hicimos una buena operación fichándole tan joven. El mercado de los '9' es complicado y podría hacer sido muy caro. Aprovechamos la oportunidad y está empezando a ofrecer dividendos". El 'Barrylete cósmico' ya está en órbita.

articles.title: De Azkargorta a Santi Denia
articles.standfirst: Seleccionadores nacidos en España que se han enfrentado a su país
articles.summary: Seleccionadores nacidos en España que se han enfrentado a su país
articles.body: La selección española no estuvo en el primer Mundial de la historia. Fue aspirante a organizarlo, pero, al igual que la mayoría de selecciones europeas, renunció a participar cuando la elegida fue Uruguay. Sin embargo, el fútbol español sí que estuvo representado en los banquillos. El seleccionador de Perú fue Paco Bru. Un fichaje rocambolesco llevó a la selección andina al entrenador que estuvo a los mandos del nacimiento de la selección española, en los Juegos de 1920. En otro equipo americano, el de México, la autoridad era el gerundense Juan Luque de Serrallonga. Después de jugar en Cádiz y Sevilla, en 1928 emigró a tierras mexicanas. Fue nombrado seleccionador y allí murió en julio de 1967. Del primer Mundial quedó su famosa arenga al equipo antes del estreno: “Muchachos, les quiero suplicar que se olviden de todo, novias, hermanos, padres, madres, y que solo les quede grabado en sus mentes la palabra México. Ahora que lucharemos contra Francia hay que recordar al general Ignacio Zaragoza. Si él pudo vencerlos, también lo podemos hacer nosotros”. México cayó 4-1. Ellos dos son los pioneros de los entrenadores españoles que han estado al mando de selecciones de otros países. Lo que hasta hace poco eran excepciones, hoy es moneda de curso común. Y no solo en selecciones exóticas, como el caso del madrileño David Pérez al frente de la selección de las Islas Vírgenes Británicas. Desde hace tiempo, los entrenadores españoles aparecen al frente de selecciones de alto nivel. Ese salto lo dio Roberto Martínez, que llevó a Bélgica a ser tercera en el Mundial de Rusia y a Portugal a ganar la Liga de las Naciones de 2026. En la súper élite actual es Xavi Hernández, a los mandos de Países Bajos, el entrenador que representa al fútbol español en los banquillos. Hoy en Praga, España se enfrenta a una selección dirigida por un entrenador que estuvo durante 15 años, de 2010 a 2025, trabajando día a día en Las Rozas. Desde el pasado verano, Santi Denia es el seleccionador de la República Checa. Al técnico del oro español en los Juegos de París le han entregado los checos las llaves de su selección para que afronte una profunda transformación. Un cambio que va más allá de la idea de juego, algo que ya resaltan los jugadores a pesar de las cuatro derrotas en el arranque de esta Liga de las Naciones. Su llegada a Praga ha llevado de la mano variaciones en todas las áreas. Por ejemplo, que un podólogo esté cerca del equipo o que las listas de convocados se den en un momento en el que la selección pueda tener la atención mediática que merece. Tras caer 3-1 en Oviedo, en un partido que se pudo poner 2-2 de no ser por un gol anulado que enfadó mucho a los checos, Denia afronta de nuevo el reto de intentar ser quien corte la asombrosa racha de España: 11 victorias, 42 partidos sin perder, que son uno más si solo se cuentan los que han tenido puntos en juego. Hasta ahora, a España se han enfrentado Camacho (1-0, con China, en 2012), Albert Roca (2-0, contra El Salvador, en 2014), David Rodrigo (4-0, con Andorra, en 2004), Roberto Martínez (Portugal, dos veces, y Bélgica) y un entrenador de cátedra: Xabier Azkargorta. Decir Azkargorta es nombrar a un entrenador idolatrado en Bolivia, el único que ha llevado a esa selección a un Mundial. Fue el de 1994. Y estuvo en el grupo de España. Es su Bigotón. “Para mí no tiene ningún sabor. Mi mayor deseo era ganar el Mundial y sigue siéndolo. Que España esté en mi grupo o no, nada tiene que ver”, explicaba el entrenador de Azpeitia antes del duelo del 27 de junio en Chicago. Las dos se podían clasificar. Ganó la selección de Clemente 3-1 en el que era el primer partido contra un seleccionador rival nacido en España. Xabier Azkargorta cambió para siempre la historia del fútbol boliviano. Más de tres décadas después, Azkargorta sigue siendo considerado en Bolivia una figura casi mítica, el entrenador que llevó a la Verde a la cima de su historia y convirtió un sueño aparentemente imposible en una realidad. Bajo su mando, Bolivia derrotó por 2-0 a Brasil en el Hernando Siles, la primera derrota de la Canarinha en una fase clasificatoria mundialista. Ocurrió el 25 de julio de 1993.

articles.title: Harry Kane's top 10 England moments as he prepares for caps record
articles.summary: BBC Sport looks at 10 of Harry Kane's most iconic England moments as he prepares to break his country's caps record.
articles.body:
Harry Kane will become England's most capped player against Croatia at Wembley on Thursday.

The 33-year-old Ballon d'Or winner has scored a record 91 goals in 125, soon to be 126, matches for his country.

England's greatest international? Kane is now a serious contender

Kane's rise from childhood keeper to equalling England cap record

Kane started his England career with a goal after just 79 seconds and three touches - in a 4-0 Euro 2016 qualifying win over Lithuania in March 2015.

Then 21 and in his first season as a Tottenham regular, he came on in the 70th minute before heading in Raheem Sterling's cross at Wembley.

The BBC match report called him "the man with the Midas touch in front of goal this season".

Kane has scored 21 major tournament goals for England, which is a record.

His first two - having failed to bag at Euro 2016 - came against Tunisia at the 2018 World Cup as captain.

He netted the opener after John Stones' header was saved and nodded in a stoppage-time winner to give England a 2-1 win in Volgograd, Russia.

Kane's first England hat-trick came in their next game, a 6-1 win over Panama in the World Cup in Nizhny Novgorod.

He scored two penalties and then deflected in Ruben Loftus-Cheek's shot for probably one of his easiest career hat-tricks.

That summer Kane became the second Englishman to win a World Cup Golden Boot, after Gary Lineker, with six goals.

The sixth was his penalty to give England a 1-0 lead over Colombia in the last 16.

Colombia equalised but Kane also scored in the shootout to help the Three Lions through.

Kane was again involved in the goals as England beat Germany in a knockout game for the first time in 55 years, to reach the Euro 2020 quarter-finals in 2021.

The striker nodded in from Jack Grealish's cross with four minutes remaining to seal a 2-0 win at Wembley.

One of the biggest goals of Kane's career was the extra-time winner over Denmark to take them into the Euro 2020 final.

His penalty was saved by Denmark's Kasper Schmeichel but the rebound came back to him to score in a 2-1 Wembley win.

That was England's first men's major tournament final since the 1966 World Cup.

Kane became England's all-time record goalscorer with his 54th goal in March 2023, taking him past Wayne Rooney, with their first away win against Italy since 1964.

He scored a first-half penalty as the Three Lions started their Euro 2024 qualifying campaign with a 2-1 win in Naples.

The striker has since extended that record by another 37 goals.

England fell behind early on in their Euro 2024 semi-final match against the Netherlands in Dortmund.

But then Kane equalised from the spot in the first half - before Ollie Watkins' last-minute winner to take them to the final.

It was his second European Championship semi-final goal in two attempts

Kane was awarded a golden cap and wore golden boots to mark his 100th England appearance in a Nations League match against Finland in 2024.

And he marked the occasion with both goals in a 2-0 win at Wembley, smashing an effort in off the underside of the bar and then curling in a second.

England's 2026 World Cup campaign almost ended with a last-32 embarrassment against DR Congo.

But Kane stepped up to save them with two goals in the final 15 minutes.

He headed in the equaliser before smashing in a brilliant winner on the turn with four minutes remaining.

In the next round he netted against Mexico and made headlines with a squeaky-voiced post-match interview in the Azteca altitude...

articles.title: Andy Robertson set to make history but hero Kenny Dalglish will always be King
articles.summary: Ties bind Scotland captain Andy Robertson and the man whose caps record he's about to equal, Kenny Dalglish, in more ways than one, writes Tom English.
articles.body:
Andy Robertson says it gives him "goosebumps" any time he thinks about it.

Friday at Hampden, North Macedonia the visitors, a 102nd cap to be won and, when it is, he'll be level in the pantheon with Sir Kenny Dalglish, the football man he loves more than any other.

On Monday in St Gallen, Switzerland - all being well - Robertson will break the great man's record, a mark that has stood for 40 years.

The Tottenham left-back is sitting in the boardroom at Queen's Park in the shadow of Hampden with a phone in his hand and eyes fixed on his 19-year-old self coming off the bench in Warsaw on 5 March, 2014.

"Nervous, excited, living the dream, not knowing what road I was on," he smiles as he looks at the moment he takes his first touch in international football.

"As I was going on, Gordon [Strachan, Scotland manager] said to me, 'remember why you're here, play like you play at Dundee United, don't play safe'. The first ball, when it came to me, I just drove forward about 30, 40 yards.

"I had pretty much every emotion that day. My mum and dad were there. My brother. My aunt and uncle. My other uncle. There's a picture of me and my brother [Stephen] at the airport after the game. He had a big Poland hat on and a half-and-half scarf. He was well oiled by that point."

Nations League: Scotland v North Macedonia

Robertson says he'd have laughed out loud had you told him then what lay ahead of him - two Premier Leagues, two League Cups, an FA Cup, a Champions League, a Super Cup, a Club World Cup, soon-to-be the most capped male Scottish players in history and, by a mile, the one with the most games as captain of the men's team.

"I've never actually been confident," he says, which is a surprise admission given everything he's done.

Maybe what he means is that he always had a quiet belief in his own ability but found that constantly questioning himself was who he was and who maybe who he still is.

"I've always doubted myself and that's always got the best out of me. I've always tried to prove people wrong and prove myself wrong. The one thing I didn't do was look too far ahead. I always just lived in the here and now and that's served me well."

In the room where he's talking there are a dozen normal chairs and away to the side, detached from the rest, is an elaborate seat. A high-backed, ornate, somewhat regal affair.

It looks fit for a king and, given the history Robertson's about to make, maybe he should plonk himself in it. And that brings us back to the man whose record he's about to match and surpass.

"There are normal seats but there's one throne and Kenny Dalglish should be sat on it," he says. "Friday night's not about me. Friday night's about the greatest player of all time in our country, and for me, that will always be Kenny.

"He's had this record for so long. He deserves it. If he played in a different era, he would probably have played a number of games that wouldn't have been able to be caught.

"Sometimes - not as a criticism - as a country we're maybe not good at recognising how good people we've got are. For me, he's the best player to ever play with Scotland and arguably Britain.

"We have to appreciate that man because I certainly do, my family certainly do and, I think on Friday, I'll have him at the front of my mind, the back of my mind and I'm not really bothered about myself."

It's a lovely thing, that. Robertson, about to draw level with Dalglish, is only thinking about Dalglish.

The depth of feeling comes tumbling out of him when he starts telling stories about what King Kenny means to his family and how he seemingly created a miracle by momentarily curing Robertson's beloved late grandfather's hearing.

"I always remember my agent talking to me about the first time he met Liverpool," Robertson says of a time when he was still with Hull but about to move to Anfield.

"He met the chief scout and sporting director and all of a sudden Kenny 'accidentally' walked into the room. It was 100% planned, I know it was planned.

'It means everything' - numbers behind Robertson's 100-cap Scotland career

You are Scotland boss Pocognoli - what would you do?

No excuses as Pocognoli seeks first Hampden victory

"One of the things right at the top of the list for me was the fact [by joining Liverpool] I got to meet Kenny in person and I've actually got to have a relationship with him and his family, because his family are special.

"My dad, in particular, has met people in football through me, but I've never seen him being starstruck by anyone apart from Kenny.

"I always remember, we'd just beaten Barcelona 4-0 [in May, 2019] to qualify for my second Champions League final. My grandad was at the game and I managed to grab Kenny afterwards. I says, 'Kenny, would you mind coming in to see my grandad and my uncle? They would love to see you'.

"Bear in mind his grandson's just qualified for another Champions League final and he basically barged me out of the way and shook Kenny's hand.

"My grandad had hearing aids. He couldn't really hear much of us but he heard everything Kenny said, so it did open a lot of questions in the family as to how bad the ear problem was with my grandad. He's no longer with us but to see how happy he was… Kenny was his hero."

When Robertson moved to Liverpool for the hilariously small sum of £8m in 2017, his wife, Rachel, was expecting their first child. The Dalglishes, he says, helped so much that he could hardly ever repay them for their support and friendship.

On the pitch and off, the transfer to Liverpool as a 23-year-old was the greatest move he could have possibly made.

In reflective mood, on the cusp of Scottish football history, Robertson talks about his mother and father and his brother. "They're as proud of my brother as they are of me," he said. "The exact same, whatever achievements we have. But I think they're more proud of the men we've become. That was always most important for me.

"Anyone who knows me, my family, my friends, I always want them to like the person first, the footballer second. Anyone that only wants to know me as the footballer, then I don't let them get too close but if they want to know me as the person first and foremost, then they're the people that are really in my close circle.

"I've still got the same friends I went to nursery with at three years old. Three of my best friends."

Inside the fairytale journey of Scotland captain Robertson

Robertson hits 100 Scotland caps - but which other men make top 10?

Robertson says he often thinks about the game in Scotland and whether young kids today are getting the kind of opportunities he got. "We talk about that - my story, John McGinn's story, Ryan Christie's story," Robertson said.

"There'll be a hundred people going, 'I could have been that'. Football has a lot to do with ability and mentality, but also you need a little bit of luck as well.

"It's about trying to protect the 15, 16, 17-year-olds just now and we all have a duty to help with that. We always want the young players to come in and I just love their energy, I love how excited they are. Findlay Curtis just bounces about all the time.

"These are the kids that are going to bring the country forward. They're all sitting at the other end of the table playing games we don't even know about but it's great for us to sit back and go, 'OK, we're part of this squad, but when we leave, then hopefully Scotland will be in a good place."

To Friday, then. A record-equaller but, to Robertson, this is no nostalgia trip. This is a game Scotland desperately want - and need - to win.

He says they were a yard off it in all areas last time out against Slovenia. "Unacceptable," he recalled. "We didn't give our fans anything to shout about."

He departs with fighting words about the desire within the squad to make amends. Out the door, down the corridor and onwards into history. Seconds later, he returns. "Forgot my washbag," he laughed. "Bet Kenny didn't have one of these!"

Glasgow, Liverpool, Scotland - the ties that bind.

articles.title: Tomas Soucek y el infierno del insomnio
articles.standfirst: Su autobiografía es un escalofriante viaje por los miedos de un deportista de élite con dos vidas: el éxito exterior y sus demonios
articles.summary: Su autobiografía es un escalofriante viaje por los miedos de un deportista de élite con dos vidas: el éxito exterior y sus demonios
articles.body: Hay futbolistas que se pasan media vida persiguiendo un sueño. Tomas Soucek lo alcanzó y, cuando parecía tenerlo todo, dejó de dormir. El capitán de la República Checa, el hombre que este jueves liderará a los suyos ante España en el Letná de Praga, relata en su autobiografía, titulada SUK, una lucha silenciosa contra el insomnio, la depresión y el miedo que durante dos años le consumieron. La imagen que proyecta Soucek invita a pensar justo lo contrario. Centrocampista poderoso, dominador del juego aéreo, líder natural dentro y fuera del campo y uno de esos jugadores que parecen indestructibles. Sin embargo, tras esa apariencia se escondía una batalla de la que apenas tuvieron noticia sus compañeros más cercanos. Ni siquiera sus padres conocían la magnitud del problema. Lo más llamativo es que la crisis no llegó cuando era un joven que buscaba abrirse camino, sino cuando ya era una figura consolidada. Jugaba en la Premier League con el West Ham United, lucía el brazalete de capitán de su selección y se había convertido en uno de los futbolistas más respetados de su país. Precisamente entonces apareció el miedo. El miedo a fallar, a no rendir, a perder aquello que tanto le había costado conseguir. “Durante dos años fui a cada partido sin dormir”, admite el capitán checo. La falta de sueño acabó convirtiéndose en una obsesión. “Intentaba dormirme tanto que terminaba sudando de rabia”, recuerda. Las noches previas a los encuentros se transformaban en un combate perdido de antemano: duchas de madrugada, horas frente a la televisión y la certeza de que el sueño no llegaría. “Pensé en poner fin a mi carrera. Me atormentaban el insomnio, la depresión y el miedo al futuro”, confiesa en una de las revelaciones más impactantes de su autobiografía. Durante ese tiempo, mientras seguía compitiendo al máximo nivel con el West Ham y la República Checa, convivió en silencio con una batalla que casi le aparta del fútbol. Buscó ayuda profesional, acudió a especialistas y terminó encontrando apoyo para superar una situación que hoy explica con naturalidad y sin esconderse. Lo hace porque entiende que visibilizar esos problemas puede ayudar a otros. Mientras libraba esa guerra interior, seguía siendo el rostro visible de la selección checa. Internacional absoluto desde 2016, suma 93 partidos y 17 goles. En el campo del Sparta, su rival porque él creció en el Slavia, se medirá por tercera vez a España. Una lesión de tobillo le dejó fuera del partido de Oviedo. Ahora, Santi Denia recupera a un jugador vital. Un tipo que ha vencido a un demonio peligroso, el que ocupó su cabeza.

articles.title: Zidane busca a su Benzema
articles.standfirst: El puesto de '9' sigue estando completamente abierto en su nueva Francia · Eli Junior Kroupi, gran novedad por la baja de Marcus Thuram
articles.summary: El puesto de '9' sigue estando completamente abierto en su nueva Francia · Eli Junior Kroupi, gran novedad por la baja de Marcus Thuram
articles.body: Karim Benzema ha tenido pocos defensores a la altura de Zinédine Zidane a lo largo de toda su carrera. Fue él, de hecho, quien le hizo entrega de su Balón de Oro en 2022. "¿El mejor delantero de la historia del fútbol francés? No me gusta decir “es el mejor”, cada uno tiene el suyo. Para mí es Karim porque trabajé con él y sé lo que vale", llegó a reconocer en 'L'Équipe'. Ahora, como seleccionador de Francia, está buscando a su nuevo Benzema. A lo largo de la historia, Francia siempre se ha caracterizado por contar con algunos de los mejores delanteros de la historia: Just Fontaine, Jean-Pierre Papin, Thierry Henry, David Trezeguet... Sin embargo, desde la retirada de Olivier Giroud de la selección, se abrió un vacío que, hasta la fecha, nadie ha terminado de rellenar. Deschamps, incluso, se vio forzado a reubicar a Mbappé como punta en los dos últimos grandes torneos de selecciones —Eurocopa 2024 y Mundial 2026— que afrontó como seleccionador nacional. Zidane, sin embargo, ya dejó claro en su estreno que quería utilizar a Kylian en la izquierda porque "es su mejor posición". Una afirmación que volvió a repetir en el momento de dar la convocatoria de cara al parón de noviembre... antes de que sufriese unas molestias que le obligarán a descansar contra Italia. Durante su primera ventana como seleccionador, Esteban Lepaul fue el único '9' puro convocado por Zidane. Era el premio a la meritocracia tras una temporada en la que había finalizado como máximo realizador de la Ligue 1 con 21 goles en las filas del Rennes. "Es un perfil diferente al que se suele ver habitualmente. Me gusta este tipo de jugador en espacios reducidos, puede ser interesante contra equipos replegados. Es un jugador que me interesa y que quiero ver de cerca". Por su movilidad y sensibilidad en las descargas, más allá de su olfato y variedad de remates en área, podía ser lo más similar a Benzema con lo que Francia cuenta en la actualidad. Zidane le ubicó de inicio en los dos partidos contra Bélgica y salió desde el banquillo contra Turquía. No vio portería... y tampoco terminó de convencer. Ahora bien, seguro que 'Zizou' quería seguir viéndole y, víctima de una lesión de tobillo, se ha quedado en casa. En los otros dos partidos, ante la propia Turquía e Italia, fue Dembélé quien ejerció como falso '9'... al igual que hace en el PSG con Luis Enrique. "Se mueve mucho, sale a menudo de su posición y eso es lo que nos interesa. Se mira mucho los goles, pero yo veo las cosas de otra manera", explicaba. Es otro, sin embargo, de los que se ha caído de su segunda lista por lesión. Ausente en su primera convocatoria, Zidane había recuperado para la causa a un Marcus Thuram a quien Deschamps dejó sin Mundial. Sin Lautaro durante este tramo más reciente del curso, dio un paso al frente en el Inter marcando seis goles y repartiendo dos asistencias... aunque es un prototipo de delantero diferente. Participa menos en el juego y brilla más en transiciones. "Es la ocasión de verlo. Tenías ganas". Sin embargo, también ha abandonado la concentración por lesión. Su sustituto ha sido un Eli Junior Kroupi que, a sus todavía 20 años, ha saltado desde la Sub21... después de haber rechazado representar a Portugal y Costa de Marfil de cara al pasado Mundial. En El Bournemouth, donde suele desempeñarse más como segundo punta por detrás de Evanilson, se erigió en la gran revelación de la pasada Premier tras registrar 13 'dianas': sensible entre líneas, incisivo y, sobre todo, con un 'francotirador' en su pie derecho. "Ya veremos si es titular en alguno de los dos partidos. Está con nosotros. Sabemos por lo que ha pasado —no debutó hasta el 25 de octubre tras sufrir una lesión en el pie —, pero está disponible. Conocemos sus cualidades. En un momento como este, está aquí y listo para jugar", exponía en la rueda de prensa previa al partido contra Italia... en el que se especula que Barcola podría arrancar como referencia. Zidane, a la espera de también recuperar a Ekitiké, sigue buscando a su Benzema.

articles.title: La hora de estar sin Messi: ¿Quién llevará la diez? ¿Quién será el capitán? ¿Quién jugará en su puesto?
articles.standfirst: La nueva Argentina arranca este sábado en la Bombonera en un amistoso ante Uruguay ya sin el mito en la convocatoria
articles.summary: La nueva Argentina arranca este sábado en la Bombonera en un amistoso ante Uruguay ya sin el mito en la convocatoria
articles.body: Ahora si, ya no hay más. Messi no está. Argentina en un amistoso ante unió de sus históricos rivales: Uruguay. El sábado en la Bombonera, se prepara para arrancar la era post con muchas dudas en el ambiente. Su primera puesta en escena real será Scaloni saltará no se podía haber elegido un estadio más simbólico, el equipo de al campo con una ausencia y muchas preguntas en el aire que deben resolverse en las próximas horas. ¿Quién llevará el 10 a la espalda? ¿Quién portará el brazalete de capitán? ¿Quién ocupará el puesto de Leo en el once titular? De hecho, la ausencia del mito ya se ha notado en la convocatoria y en el cuartel general de la albiceleste para preparar el partido. "Tenemos que acostumbrarnos a su ausencia", comentaba a los periodistas argentinos un destacado miembro del nunca 10 fue, casi desde que debutó su aura equipo nada más pisar las instalaciones. Messi no era uno más, y a la falta era una constante, su motivación, su jerarquía casi sin abrir la boca. Ahora Argentina empieza una nueva andadura del líder se unen las dudas futbolísticas que plantea la nueva era. ¿Será capaz la 'scaloneta' de arrancar sin el motor y el alma? Esa pregunta está en el aire y otras también trascendentales también. ¿Quién llevará el 10 a la espalda? De momento, si no hay cambio de última hora, hay muchos candidatos jóvenes y algún que otro veterano, pero en esta dupla de partidos amistosos, al no haber obligación de cubrir el dorsal, la decisión es que no haya portador. Se esperará a los partidos oficiales. Otra de las cuestiones, esta sí con respuesta oficial, está en la mente de todos. ¿Qué jugador asumirá la capitanía? si se recupera de las molestias (ayer ya trabajó con el resto del grupo e hizo portería) será el Dibu Martínez el que ejerza de capitán de la albiceleste. El actual portero del Chelsea tiene galones de sobra para llevar el brazalete y si está sobre el campo será el que lo lleve en el brazo. La última pregunta solo la puede desvelar el propio Scaloni. ¿Quién hará de Messi sobre el terreno de juego? Hay varios candidatos, pero en Argentina se señala a Julián Álvarez para ocupar la zona de Leo sobre el campo. El jugador del Atlético es el mejor colocado para intentar que la ausencia de Messi sobre el campo se note lo menos posible. Aunque es tarea imposible, alguien tiene que asumir el reto y empezar de cero. Otras muchas preguntas irán encontrando respuesta con el tiempo. ¿Quién dará la charla en el vestuario? ¿A quién buscarán los jugadores cuando la cosa se complique durante el juego? ¿Quién será el primero en saltar al campo liderando al grupo? La era post Messi arranca en Argentina, algo para lo que la selección lleva años preparándose y para lo que obviamente, no está preparada.

articles.title: Mikel Arteta's hunger for Arsenal to retain the Premier League can help them defy the odds and maintain their standards
articles.summary: The challenge of retaining the title is a difficult one physically and mentally but there are specific reasons why Mikel Arteta's Arsenal are built to last and the manager's awareness of the psychology behind it can help them sustain their success, argues Adam Bate
articles.body:
"That's when everybody's ego rears its head and the uncanny chemistry the team felt just a few months earlier suddenly dissolves into thin air," argues Jackson. He quotes Rick Fox, three-time NBA champion turned actor, who compared it to winning an Oscar.

"It defines who you are," he says. "For the rest of your life you mean something." That kind of self-worth can be a valuable commodity and a useful tool in unlocking even greater potential in an individual. "But it also changes your expectations," adds Jackson.

He goes on to quote Fox further: "You win a championship and you all go away and get patted on the back for several months. Then you return for the new season and you're saying, 'This is what I want to happen for me.'" That can be a problem in any team sport.

Earlier this year, Arsenal became Premier League champions for the first time in 22 years. It was an accomplishment that Mikel Arteta and all at the club had ached for so much that the tension could sometimes be felt on the pitch let alone in the stands.

The catharsis was real but the challenge for Arteta was to ensure that it did not feel like an ending for his Arsenal team. For a number of reasons, the signs already are that this Gunners side are not going to succumb to the insidious issues Jackson warned about.

Targets help. And Arsenal's history provides easy motivational tools. First of all, this great football club, for all its success, did not retain the title under Bertie Mee, George Graham or Arsene Wenger. Indeed, no Arsenal manager has ever achieved the feat.

Their 1930s threepeat came under three different managers with Herbert Chapman's passing leading to Joe Shaw serving as caretaker for the second title win before George Allison replaced him for the third. For Arteta, in particular, it would be some honour.

For the team as a whole, the Champions League final defeat to Paris Saint-Germain was anything but welcome. But one wonders whether that too has helped to avoid any sense of finality to their mission. The mood in Budapest so quickly shifted to one of defiance.

"We are going to use this moment to fuel us for the upcoming seasons - speaking to the players and the manager, there is no reason why we are stopping here," said Declan Rice. "Next year, we are going to go even stronger and we are going to be ready again."

Ten games into the Premier League season and Arsenal are five points clear at the top of the table and odds-on to retain the title. In the Champions League standings, they are third and unbeaten. They boast the best defensive record in both competitions.

In other words, there is no hint of lost purpose. Arteta's Asenal remain fully focused. And given his awareness of the importance of psychology, one can be that their manager has been the architect of all the mood music around the club. For him, the job is not done.

The branding around the stadium declaring Arsenal champions came down quickly and it was surely no coincidence that the two most expensive signings of the summer - Bruno Guimaraes and Ezri Konsa - were experiences players yet to win the biggest prizes.

Even the signing of Arteta's contract extension was utilised as an opportunity to reinforce the message. "What is so exciting is that this is only the beginning of what we can achieve together," he said after signing that new four-year deal with the club in October.

That framing drew a reaction from Jose Mourinho. "I saw something interesting that would not happen at Real Madrid. Mikel Arteta renewed his contract and said something like, 'We are still starting, this is just the beginning.' And he has been there for years."

Mourinho's comments are understandable given that next month marks the seventh anniversary of Arteta's reign. He is already the longest-serving manager in English football, having been in the job three years longer than any other Premier League boss.

But perhaps Arteta just understands the importance of shaping the narrative - and the dangers that come when the protagonists believe that the mountain has been climbed. His Arsenal are still striving for more. And as long as they are, more can be achieved.

articles.title: La Roma toma una decisión con Balde: Moretto desvela sus prioridades
articles.standfirst: El periodista italiano asegura en La Pizarra de Quintana que el futbolista azulgrana está cada vez más abierto a marcharse y aclara el interés de la Roma
articles.summary: El periodista italiano asegura en La Pizarra de Quintana que el futbolista azulgrana está cada vez más abierto a marcharse y aclara el interés de la Roma
articles.body: El futuro de Alejandro Balde podría estar lejos del Barcelona. Matteo Moretto ha analizado en La Pizarra de Quintana, de Radio MARCA, la situación del futbolista azulgrana, que no está teniendo el protagonismo esperado y empieza a plantearse una salida en el próximo mercado de invierno. El periodista italiano también ha hablado del futuro de Endrick, uno de los nombres que maneja la Roma para reforzar su plantilla. "Balde puede salir en enero del Barça y está más abierto a salir. Tiene claro que no va a tener un sitio fijo en la plantilla, no está teniendo minutos ni protagonismo. El chico se lo está pensando más", ha explicado Moretto sobre la situación del defensa azulgrana. El periodista también ha aclarado las informaciones que relacionaban al futbolista con la Roma. "Balde fue relacionado a un club de Italia, que es la Roma y yo conozco muy bien... Y la Roma tiene otras prioridades", ha señalado. De hecho, ha insistido en que "la Roma tiene como prioridad fichar delanteros, no defensa", por lo que el conjunto italiano tiene otros objetivos en el mercado. Uno de esos objetivos es Endrick. El delantero brasileño del Real Madrid también podría cambiar de aires en enero y Moretto considera que su salida es cada vez más probable. "Creo que Endrick no lo tiene decidido 100% si salir o no, pero para mí tiene más pinta de salir que de quedarse", ha asegurado. Una situación que contrasta con la postura de José Mourinho. "Aunque Mourinho siempre dice que es importante y tiene que quedarse. Depende mucho de lo que quiere el Real Madrid, pero en este caso depende más de lo que quiere Endrick", ha explicado el periodista, que ha añadido: "Para mí, mezcla de información y sensación, es que va a salir". En cuanto a los posibles destinos, Moretto ha señalado al conjunto italiano como principal candidato: "La Roma es el mejor posicionado, pero el Inter también le quiere y otros equipos de la Premier". Además, el periodista ha destacado el papel que puede desempeñar Carlo Ancelotti en la decisión del brasileño. "Ancelotti le va a aconsejar", ha afirmado antes de desvelar una información sobre la postura del entrenador madridista: "Lo que puedo confirmar al 100% es que cuando Mourinho salió y dijo que Endrick se iba a quedar seguro yo averigüé que no iba a ser así".

articles.title: Michael Carrick sacked: Man Utd boss goes from signing two-year deal to being sacked 15 games later
articles.summary: Michael Carrick becomes the third Manchester United manager to be sacked in three seasons - where did it go wrong?
articles.body:
It was just after 6pm on Sunday, 8 November when the message landed. Manchester United were 4-2 down to Aston Villa, and Old Trafford was resigned to defeat.

The plea came from someone who knows Michael Carrick well, has worked with him and understands at first hand the pressures of life in the United goldfish bowl.

As it turned out, the predicted ending did not come to pass.

United scored twice in stoppage time to salvage a 4-4 draw. Carrick celebrated Patrick Dorgu's equaliser by raising an arm in the air. After that, he walked round the pitch on what has turned out to be a final lap of appreciation.

As the United supporters sang his name, Carrick placed himself in the middle of his players to ensure the fans did not turn on them in the way they had done after the 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth two weeks before.

It was a decision that summed up the 45-year-old - supporting the collective, rather than looking after himself.

That obvious desire to do the best for his club and his players - and his storied past - explains why Carrick's song continued to be bellowed from the stands when just about everyone else involved at United was attracting fury and derision.

To get this far is longer than many envisaged. It seemed there was no way Carrick could survive the Bournemouth debacle.

United took 44 hours to communicate to the wider world they were sticking with him then, though it is understood Carrick was told the day before.

Since then, it has been chaos. United have won one, drawn one and lost one.

Outstanding in the opening 45 minutes at Chelsea, they conceded at the start of the second half before defender Lisandro Martinez was sent off for two bookings in the space of five minutes. They lost 2-0.

Awful and two goals down inside 17 minutes against Roma in the Champions League, they roared back with the kind of thrilling comeback Carrick was part of so often during Sir Alex Ferguson's days to win 3-2.

Then, Villa. Two goals down in four minutes thanks to calamitous goalkeeping, they clawed back to level before half-time. More abysmal defending left United with another mountain to climb - but they emerged from the carnage with a point.

Try picking the bones out of that. Had Carrick's stock increased, or had it merely proven he was not the right man the job? United decided it was the latter.

Chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox celebrated Dorgu's stoppage-time equaliser against Villa in the directors' box. But they had a slightly detached perspective.

Within days they were flying to Monaco to tell minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe change was required.

For the third season in a row, United are replacing the man in charge of the team mid-season.

Unlike with Erik ten Hag and Ruben Amorim, this decision is not a surprise. Not because of what is happening now, but because what is happening now is so at odds with what happened last season.

After 12 wins in 17 games under Carrick and a return to the Champions League, the mood in pre-season was overwhelmingly positive.

There were no signs of splits, young players including JJ Gabriel were part of the group, and senior staff spoke optimistically about the potential of Bruno Fernandes' proposed partnership with Youri Tielemans.

Recruitment was clearly an issue, but more of that later.

Defeats and outbursts - Man Utd's season unravels

Looking back, the 48 hours before United's season-opening match at Hull were pivotal.

With Benjamin Sesko still trying to ease his way back from the shin issue that ended his previous campaign early, Amad Diallo suffered an ankle injury that would rule him out for seven weeks. It meant Carrick was deprived of his first-choice striking alternative, with Bryan Mbeumo having to play on the right of the attack.

Carrick instead turned to Matheus Cunha, whose preference for dropping deep took him into the spaces captain Fernandes likes to occupy.

It neutralised United's attack on a day they seemed ill-prepared to meet the physical challenge of an opponent motivated by their long-awaited Premier League return.

In his role as interviewer for Nordic broadcaster Viaplay, former Norway and Middlesbrough striker Jan Aage Fjortoft claimed United had lacked passion - something Carrick dismissed as "ridiculous".

"It's one game," Carrick told the media afterwards.

The following week, United were losing to Ipswich - another newly promoted side. Only a slip from Marcelino Nunez inside his own half allowed Cunha to tee up Fernandes for an undeserved equaliser. Fernandes, who had just been crowned PFA Player of the Year for 2025-26, went on to complete a hat-trick in a 5-2 win.

United have not won in the Premier League since.

After that came a trip to Everton. Twice United led, the second time when Sesko struck two minutes from time after coming on as a substitute. Deep into stoppage time, Ainsley Maitland-Niles drove home from long range to deny the visitors.

Asked how confident he was in his side's ability to react to a disappointing start to the season, Carrick snapped back: "It's not been that bad."

Time and again, United's fitness was called into question. They struggled badly against a Manchester City side reduced to 10 men in the first half before City benefited from an Erling Haaland goal that referees' chief Howard Webb later admitted should not have stood.

Carrick's complaints after the match were justified - but they masked a poor performance from his team.

After taking a 2-0 lead inside 10 minutes against Brighton in the EFL Cup, United were outplayed and beaten, thanks to two goals in four second-half minutes.

Carrick's coaching staff - lauded months earlier - could not find an answer.

The head coach said Cunha's injury-time equaliser against a Fulham side who started the game bottom was a positive to build on. But immediately after the international break, United were held to another draw - conceding in injury time to an out-of-form and 10-man Tottenham.

The familiar downward spiral was getting out of control.

Martinez was at fault for Spurs' leveller, which made his post-match outburst after the 2-0 Champions League defeat by Atletico Madrid more amazing.

The Argentina defender criticised United's summer recruitment and placed the blame at the door of "the technical director" - Wilcox.

By the time of Martinez's outburst, Sesko and left-back Luke Shaw were injured. Marcus Rashford has not played since. The rotation at left-back eventually led to Carrick starting five different players in that role.

After conceding in the opening minute against Atletico, Como scored inside the first two in a 4-1 win. Fernandes came out afterwards and criticised Carrick's tactics.

He was dropped for the Bournemouth game, but returned as captain at Chelsea.

There is no doubt Carrick made mistakes. The Hull game - a performance that set the tone for the season so far - was inexplicable.

But it is also fair to wonder how much he was let down by the recruitment side.

A source close to one player questioned why so much attention was focused on midfield, when the inevitable consequence was Fernandes being shifted away from the central position he excelled in over the second half of last season.

Casemiro's exit necessitated a big-money replacement but, after heading down one-way streets in the pursuit of Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest and Mateus Fernandes from West Ham, it was 25 August before the £70m deal to sign Carlos Baleba from Brighton was completed.

A pre-existing ankle injury meant Baleba did not make his debut until 10 October. After starting only five games, he is now out for an extended period with a hamstring problem.

Tielemans arrived from Aston Villa for £35m and Andrey Santos signed from Chelsea in a deal that could eventually cost £50m. The former scored his first goal in the Villa thriller. Santos, though, was left on the bench. He has started four league games.

Meanwhile, obvious issues in Carrick's squad were left unaddressed.

Shaw started every Premier League game last season, but that was an outlier in an otherwise injury-hit career. Clear competition was needed in that area. Instead, United backed off, thinking they might be able to sign Lewis Hall from Newcastle next summer.

United's back four for the first home game of the season was the same as it was for the first home game under Ten Hag in 2022. They have conceded 30 goals so far this term - the most of any team in Europe's top five leagues, apart from Lens.

Up front, Sesko finished last season injured and had only made two substitute appearances when the transfer window closed. Carrick subsequently admitted he would be out for a "long time" - thought to be at least January.

Carrick was asked about the possibility of further signings following the arrivals of Tielemans and Santos during the club's pre-season training camp on 13 August.

"We want more, we need more," was the response.

For someone so calm and considered, it was a strong demand for action to those above. Well-placed sources say it was obvious to Carrick where the holes in his squad were and he was expecting more than a single new signing from that point.

A couple of weeks before Carrick spoke, another club source told BBC Sport that United should be judged when the transfer window closed.

From this position, that judgement would have to be negative.

However, other United sources defend the recruitment strategy, claiming it easy to be wise after the event and at the end of last season, Kobbie Mainoo was their only orthodox midfield option.

It is also argued the United squad is capable of finishing in the Champions League places.

More than a quarter of the way into the season, they are some way off that target.

Carrick has paid the price - lasting less than six months into the two-year contract he signed in May.

Mauricio Pochettino looks likely to be his replacement. Berrada and Wilcox will hope his appointment brings calm after another period of chaos.

articles.title: Man Utd sack Michael Carrick with Mauricio Pochettino set to be appointed after worst start to Premier League season
articles.summary: Michael Carrick has been sacked by Man Utd less than six months after signing a two-year deal; USA boss Mauricio Pochettino has reached an agreement take over after Carrick oversaw United's worst-ever Premier League start; United are in the relegation zone after 10 league games
articles.body:
Carrick departs less than six months after signing a two-year contract having overseen the club's worst start to a Premier League season with United in the relegation zone after picking up one win in 10 matches.

In a statement on Thursday morning, shortly after Carrick left the training ground, United said they reached "the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions".

United, who reached a full agreement with USA head coach Pochettino , say they intend to appoint a permanent successor "as quickly as possible". He is set to be the eighth permanent appointment since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013.

As things stand, the Argentine is likely to remain in charge of the USA for their Nations League against Haiti on Saturday and Wednesday before starting work next Thursday. He is expected to take charge of United's first game after the international break against Liverpool.

Sky Sports News understands Pochettino has a £7m release clause in his newly-signed contract with the USA. Talks with the United Soccer Federation are at the "paperwork and regulatory processes" stage.

Carrick took training in Manchester on Wednesday as United reached a verbal agreement with Pochettino.

Meanwhile, club chiefs were at a Monaco summit with minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe. That is where the decision to sack Carrick was ratified by Ratcliffe following the recommendation of chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox.

United's hierarchy, including Wilcox and Berrada, are understood to feel that the current squad is much better than results and performances have shown.

Carrick's exit follows United's 4-4 draw against Aston Villa on Sunday , when they fell 2-0 down inside four minutes and then 4-2 down early in the second half before mounting a last-gasp comeback to draw.

The rescue job followed a similar turnaround to beat Roma in the Champions League last Tuesday but was not enough to convince the United hierarchy to continue with the former midfielder in charge.

Jonny Evans and Jonathan Woodgate, who were part of the coaching set up under Carrick, will also leave the club along with Steve Holland, Travis Binnion and goalkeeping coach Craig Mawson.

The only coach who remains is assistant first-team goalkeeping coach Connor King who joined the club two months ago.

Carrick was initially appointed as United boss in January 2026 on a contract until the end of the season , following Ruben Amorim's sacking earlier in that campaign. He delivered a brilliant run of results, winning 12 of 17 matches to earn a third-place finish in the Premier League and a return to the Champions League.

Carrick was nominated for Premier League Manager of the Season and, on May 22, signed a new contract running to 2028. However, just three wins in 15 matches this term have cost him his job.

Former Tottenham, Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain boss Pochettino has been considered for the United job on three previous occasions, but finally now looks set for the Old Trafford hot seat.

Neville: United need bigger solution than sacking Carrick

"You can keep changing the manager and thinking that's going to be the answer. But this has been proven now over 12 years, that's not the answer.

"It's rinse and repeat. Ruben Amorim, Erik ten Hag, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, Carrick, Jose Mourinho, Louis van Gaal, David Moyes, Ralf Rangnick - some of them are world-class managers who have had success. There are a lot of promising young managers there, ex-players who know the club as well.

"None of it has worked because if you've got a poor performance department, poor recruitment department, you've not got leadership that is strong right through the spine of the football club you will fail."

United won 12 out of 17 games last season under Carrick - a 70.1 per cent win rate , which saw him comfortably sit with the best record of permanent Old Trafford managers.

But he leaves with a record of 15 wins in 32 matches - a rate of just 46.9 per cent , which leaves him only ahead of Ruben Amorim, the man he replaced in the dugout last season, in the years since Ferguson's retirement.

Carrick has overseen three wins in 15 matches this campaign (20 per cent). They won eight out of 21 games before Amorim's sacking last year (38.1 per cent).

His dropoff brings echoes of Ole Gunnar Solskjaer. The former United striker's win percentage fell from 73.7 per cent as interim manager (14 wins in 19 games) to 51.7 per cent having been appointed on a permanent basis (77 out of 149).

Carrick had three games as caretaker boss after Solskjaer's departure, wins over Villarreal and Arsenal and a draw with Chelsea. These matches are not counted towards his record as permanent manager.

Ferguson's shadow Since the retirement in 2013 of Ferguson, who won 26 major trophies in 27 years at Old Trafford and had a 59.7 per cent win ratio, United have struggled to find a long-term figurehead.

Ferguson took charge of 1,500 games with United. In 731 games since he retired in 2013, Carrick was the club's seventh permanent manager in addition to interim boss Ralf Rangnick and caretakers Ryan Giggs, Carrick himself, Ruud van Nistelrooy and Darren Fletcher.

Jose Mourinho has the best win percentage of those permanent managers, with 58.3 per cent , 84 out of 144 games.

Mourinho also won the most trophies of any manager since Ferguson, with a League Cup and Europa League double in 2016-17 having opened that season with the Community Shield.

Erik ten Hag won both domestic cups, Louis van Gaal lifted an FA Cup and David Moyes another Community Shield.

Timeline: INEOS' time in charge at Man Utd so far

December 2023: Sir Jim Ratcliffe's deal to purchase a stake in United is announced.

January 2024: United appoint Omar Berrada from rivals Manchester City as their new chief executive. The move was made by Ratcliffe in consultation with Joel and Avram Glazer but INEOS were the driving force behind the move.

February 2024: Ratcliffe completes deal to acquire 27.7 per cent stake in Manchester United, which gives his company, INEOS, control of football operations.

April 2024: INEOS and Ratcliffe shake-up continued as United appoint Jason Wilcox as technical director after less than a year as director of football at Southampton, which was his first executive role in senior football.

July 2024: Man Utd agree deal with Newcastle United to appoint Dan Ashworth as sporting director after a lengthy period of gardening leave.

July 2024: Erik ten Hag is handed a one-year contract extension after winning the FA Cup by beating Manchester City 2-1 in the final. He is backed with the signings of Matthijs De Ligt, Noussair Mazraoui, Joshua Zirkzee, Manuel Ugarte and Leny Yoro.

July 2024: Christopher Vivell is hired as director of global talent on a temporary basis.

October 2024: United sack manager Ten Hag after winning just four of their 14 games to start the 2024/25 season. United in 14th and Ruud van Nistelrooy appointed as interim boss.

November 2024: Ruben Amorim is confirmed as the club's new head coach, signing a contract until June 2027. United paid £9.2m to release him from Sporting.

December 2024: Ashworth leaves his role as sporting director after just five months. He oversaw a £200m spend in the transfer market.

December 2024: Wilcox steps into Ashworth's role as sporting director.

February 2025: Vivell is appointed as permanent director of recruitment.

June 2025: Wilcox is promoted to director of football after Sir Dave Brailsford ends association with the club. He is tasked with overseeing football operations, including recruitment.

January 5 2026: Amorim is sacked after 14 months in charge after winning only 24 of his 63 games in charge. Darren Fletcher is appointed as interim boss.

January 13 2026: Michael Carrick is appointed as head coach until the end of the 2025/26 season.

May 2026: After securing Champions League football and winning 12 of his 17 games in charge, Carrick is rewarded with a two-year deal at Old Trafford.

November 12 2026: Carrick leaves United following a draw with Aston Villa, which left the club in the Premier League relegation zone after 10 games.

Michael Carrick has been sacked as Manchester United head coach , so how did his Old Trafford reign go so wrong, so quickly?

The former midfielder guided United to a Champions League finish last season but after their worst start to a season in 40 years, they are in the Premier League relegation zone at the start of November.

United salvaged a 4-4 draw against Aston Villa in Carrick's final game in charge, but they have only won once in 10 Premier League fixtures so far despite finishing last term on a high, with former Spurs and Chelsea boss Mauricio Pochettino set to take over.

articles.title: Manchester United sack Michael Carrick as manager
articles.summary: Carrick exits after United drop to 18th in Premier League table; he led them to three wins across all competitions.
articles.body:
Manchester United have sacked manager Michael Carrick, the Premier League club confirmed in a statement, amid a torrid time for the global football giants, who find themselves in the league’s relegation zone.

Carrick’s departure, which had been imminent after United made their worst start to the English top flight in 40 years, was announced on Thursday by the club, which said it would “appoint a permanent successor as quickly as possible”.

“Manchester United can confirm that Michael Carrick has departed his role as men’s first-team head coach”, the Old Trafford club said in a statement.

“After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions.”

United, 13-time Premier League champions, have been heavily linked with US Men’s National Team coach Mauricio Pochettino .

Pochettino – whose release from the contract extension he signed as USA head coach has reportedly been arranged – would become the eighth permanent man in charge at Old Trafford since Sir Alex Ferguson’s departure in May 2013 after more than 26 years in the job.

United’s statement termed Carrick a club legend.

“Just as he [Carrick] did as a player, he has conducted himself with the highest standards of dedication and professionalism throughout his time back with the club,” the statement added.

“His leadership and achievements last season will always be fondly remembered.”

The 45-year-old’s last game as United’s head coach ended in a dramatic late draw against Aston Villa at Old Trafford, where the furious home fans voiced their anger towards the club’s ownership.

United needed a stoppage-time equaliser to eke out a point against 10th-placed Villa, but it was not enough to lift them out of the Premier League’s relegation zone.

The Red Devils briefly dropped to the bottom of the table before results elsewhere in the league took them back to 18th place with eight points from their 10 games this season.

Carrick, who was handed the United job on an interim basis in January , knew his managerial position was under threat following a series of disappointing results in recent weeks.

United have endured four losses and five draws, with their solitary win coming against Ipswich Town in late August.

They were also knocked out of the English League Cup in the third round, and have made an unconvincing start in their Champions League campaign, with two wins and as many losses.

Overall, United have won only three times in 15 games across all competitions this season.

Carrick’s sacking marks the end of a rollercoaster reign at the club.

The former United midfielder, who also captained the club in his final season as a player, took over from the sacked Ruben Amorim last term, when the team were seventh, but lifted them to a third-place finish and secured Champions League qualification at the end of the 2025-26 season.

The players looked like a better, more exciting version of themselves under Carrick when he first took over, but fans’ optimism vanished when the revival did not continue into the current campaign.

United’s defeat to newly-promoted Hull City in their opening match of the league season marked an embarrassing start for the former champions. What followed was further humiliation on and off the field, with a dressing room rift damaging Carrick’s image, and the club’s hierarchy losing faith in one of their own.

British media have linked several high-profile managers to the job.

Newcastle United boss Eddie Howe and ex-Germany coach Julian Nagelsmann were among the frontrunners, but USA men’s national team coach Mauricio Pochettino has seemingly overtaken both as favourite.

Pochettino, who previously took charge of Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea in the English top flight, has been widely favoured by US and British media.

Former Chelsea coach Antonio Conte is also in the running.

A managerial change is expected during this international break, with a new face likely to lead United on their trip to Anfield to face longtime rivals, Liverpool, on November 22.

articles.title: Manchester United fires Michael Carrick as head coach, lines up US coach Mauricio Pochettino
articles.summary: Manchester United has fired embattled head coach Michael Carrick after a dire start to the season that leaves the once-great club languishing in the Premier League relegation zone.
articles.body: Manchester United has fired embattled head coach Michael Carrick after a dire start to the season that leaves the once-great club languishing in the Premier League relegation zone. It’s not yet confirmed who will take over from the Englishman, but CNN Sports understands that US Men’s National Team (USMNT) coach Mauricio Pochettino has reached a verbal agreement with the club. The club said it “intends to appoint a permanent successor as quickly as possible.” Carrick took over on an interim basis in January before overseeing a turnaround in the squad’s fortunes at the tail end of the last campaign. That resurgence was enough to earn him the permanent job in May, when he signed a two-year contract with the club he once played for. However, this season has quickly turned sour, with the team winning just once in 10 Premier League matches – the club’s worst league start in 40 years. “After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions,” a club statement said Thursday. “Michael is, and always will be, a Manchester United legend. Just as he did as a player, he has conducted himself with the highest standards of dedication and professionalism throughout his time back with the club. His leadership and achievements last season will always be fondly remembered.” In addition to the shocking run of results, which leaves the Red Devils in 18th place, the season has been punctuated by several flashpoints – including public outbursts from club captain Bruno Fernandes and fans turning on many of the players. Carrick becomes the seventh permanent head coach to be sacked by United since the departure of legendary manager Alex Ferguson in 2013. In truth, Carrick’s departure had been expected for much of this week, with reports emerging that the club’s hierarchy was due to meet in Monaco on Wednesday to make it official. Meanwhile, Carrick took training as normal, even when it was clear who United was lining up as his potential replacement. Talks between United, Pochettino and US Soccer will continue this week before anything is made official. The USMNT is set to play Haiti on Saturday and Tuesday and, as things stand, Pochettino is expected to be in charge of both matches before any move to Old Trafford. Who is Mauricio Pochettino? So, what do we know about Pochettino and will he be a good fit at Manchester United? Before management, Pochettino was a very good player – representing the likes of Spanish side Espanyol and French giant Paris Saint-Germain (PSG). He also represented his country, Argentina, including at the 2002 World Cup. But it was as a manager that he really flourished. He started back at his former club Espanyol, but began making a real name for himself while impressing at English club Southampton. A move to Tottenham followed in 2014 where he transformed the team into a winning machine. He most notably led the London club to the UEFA Champions League final in 2019, before losing to Liverpool. By this point, the Argentine was considered one of the best coaches in the world – known for developing young talent, a front-foot style of play and a no-nonsense approach to management. Spells at PSG and Chelsea followed before he took charge of the USA in 2024. And while his project took a while to get going, he led the US team to an impressive World Cup campaign and the team now looks well set for the future. Interestingly, Pochettino has been on United’s radar before but, for whatever reason, the two parties could never quite line up. Now, though, Pochettino has the chance to bring United back to the top of the sport. Analysis: Can Manchester United finally get something right? This week has been another lowlight for Manchester United. News of the club’s hierarchy meeting in Monaco on Wednesday to recommend replacing Carrick created an unnecessary saga that dragged the club legend through the wringer. While reports of his imminent sacking were allowed to spread like wildfire, Carrick kept his head down and took training as normal – sticking to his philosophy and looking like the only adult in the room. The handling of his departure was just another example of how poorly the club is being run, and puts the spotlight firmly on the ownership once again. Things were supposed to be so different. When co-owner Jim Ratcliffe and INEOS took charge of the soccer operations a few years ago, their arrival was going to breathe fresh life into a club decaying under the much-maligned Glazer family’s ownership. And, in truth, there was an initial injection of excitement. The club got a revamped training facility, plans for a new stadium were announced and a new management structure was established, making Omar Berrada the CEO and Jason Wilcox the sporting director. The two were supposed to overhaul the squad and usher in a new era of success – with an initial goal to win the Premier League in 2028. Only, in reality, almost everything has gone wrong since. Carrick is the third head coach to fail under their watch, following Erik ten Hag and Ruben Amorim. Millions have been spent on compensation to fix those mistakes and performances have suffered. The club now looks set to secure the man they call “Poch,” a manager they’ve been interested in but ultimately overlooked in recent seasons. But whether it’s Pochettino or someone else who eventually takes charge, the job facing the new head coach is gigantic. First, they have to work out how to fit into the club’s failing hierarchy. They’ll then need to work on a playing roster that looks short of quality and motivate players who look mentally fragile. Perhaps most importantly, the new boss will need to keep the fans on side. Even when things got ugly under Carrick, the supporters chose to back the former midfielder, putting the blame firmly at the feet of the players and the club’s hierarchy. The consensus is that the current culture around the club is so toxic that it’s almost impossible for any head coach to succeed. The new manager will have a tough job trying to prove that wrong. This story has been updated with additional information.
