articles.title: Michael Carrick sacked by Man Utd: How his Old Trafford reign unravelled in worst start to a season in 40 years
articles.summary: Michael Carrick has been sacked as Man Utd boss after their 4-4 draw with Aston Villa left them in the relegation zone; former midfielder was appointed on temporary basis in January and got permanent job in May; Man Utd stormed to third last term so what went wrong?
articles.body:
The former midfielder guided United to a Champions League finish last season but after their worst start to a season in 40 years, they are in the Premier League relegation zone at the start of November.

United salvaged a 4-4 draw against Aston Villa in Carrick's final game in charge, but they have only won once in 10 Premier League fixtures so far despite finishing last term on a high, with former Spurs and Chelsea boss Mauricio Pochettino set to take over.

Carrick's impact was immediate after taking over in January. The visit of Manchester City to Old Trafford looked a difficult start but a 2-0 win proved a launchpad. "One of the best performances you'll see in any era by a United team," said Gary Neville.

United followed it up with wins over Arsenal, Fulham and Tottenham. It was the first time they had won four straight Premier League games in two years. The mood was transformed.

The club were seventh when Carrick took over. By the end of the season, he had taken them back into the Champions League in third, completing an unlikely turnaround which earned him a nomination for the Premier League Manager of the Year award.

Between his appointment in January and the end of the campaign, Manchester United took more points than even champions Arsenal, with 39, winning 12 out of 17 Premier League games having only won eight of the first 21 in the first half of the campaign.

Carrick's most impactful change was to do away with Ruben Amorim's favoured back three system, allowing him to move Bruno Fernandes from the base of midfield, where he had looked a poor fit alongside Casemiro, back into his favoured No 10 role.

The result was an explosion in his creative output. Fernandes' open-play creativity rose by 81 per cent under Carrick as he broke the Premier League assists record for a single season and ended up as both the PFA and FWA Player of the Year.

"Michael came in with a big personality but also with a lot of calmness about what he needed to do to bring the best out of the team," Fernandes told Sky Sports in May.

The same player would end up being a protagonist in his downfall.

Underwhelming window, pre-season worries

United's return to the Champions League, secured with three games of last season to spare, was a triumph for Carrick. The former midfielder was made permanent head coach before finishing the campaign with a 3-0 win away to Brighton on the final day.

But the return to European competition also heightened the need to strengthen the squad in the summer. Carrick had the luxury of a light schedule last season but that was about the change with the addition of a minimum of eight extra games.

The club spent £163m in the window, less than newly-promoted Hull and Ipswich, and chose to invest it all in one area of the pitch only, prioritising the midfield with the signings of Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba. The latter arrived injured.

Three months on, the trio are yet to offer value for money. Meanwhile, the lack of investment in other areas has been punished.

They continue to look short of quality in defence, where player turnover has been minimal, while Benjamin Sesko's injury issues have left them without a proper No 9 for most of the season.

Tielemans' revelation that there hadn't been a focus on fitness work during pre-season rang alarm bells in August and the side's sluggish displays subsequently raised questions of their conditioning.

"The reality is they're not running enough, they're not showing enough tenacity, determination, fighting spirit. They're just not," said Neville after their 1-1 draw with 10-man Spurs, doubling down on similar comments made after the draw with Fulham.

Carrick argued otherwise but tracking data puts United among the Premier League's bottom clubs for both distance covered and sprints this season. Their lack of intensity allowed a string of opponents to overpower them with ease.

Defeat to Hull on the opening day set the tone for the new campaign. A meagre total of seven points from their first seven games made it United's worst start in 40 years.

Their only victory, a 5-2 win over Ipswich at Old Trafford, also stands out as the only Premier League game in which Fernandes had either scored or assisted before his penalty against Aston Villa on Sunday. His loss of form proved especially damaging for Carrick. Soon, it seemed tensions were spilling over.

"We had a fantastic season last season, and now we expect more from the top, from upstairs, to bring in more players to compete because many teams have brought in many players as well.

"I expect more from our technical director. I have to be honest. And also, as a player, we have to do more. But it's also important to build a strong squad to be ready for this kind of night."

Martinez also appeared critical of Carrick. "He does his best," he said. "But every season is different. You can't stay with what you did last season. The teams know how you play, they know every detail. If you don't change, next season is a big problem."

Those comments were nothing, though, compared to those made by Fernandes after the loss to Como, when he questioned Carrick and his staff directly over their plan for United's pressing.

"It's a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave a little space in behind and try to get the ball in the first moment, to wait for them, to give them the ball," he said.

"But sometimes when you give the ball to these teams, they get confident, they have so many bodies behind the ball that make you run a lot, make people get frustrated, and when you recover the ball the legs and the brain are more difficult to make work."

Carrick responded when the comments of his captain were put to him. "We half pressed man-to-man in the second half and ended up conceding a goal from that," he said. "Whatever tactics you play, if you don't run back, you ain't going to win."

Carrick later insisted there was no divide between the players and the coaching staff. Fernandes later described reports of their relationship becoming strained as "lies". But from that moment on it seemed a question of when, not if, the head coach would depart.

Fernandes was recalled to the team after his omission from the 3-0 loss to Bournemouth and scored his first Premier League goal since August in the draw with Aston Villa. But the player who inspired their turnaround under Carrick last season could not do enough to save him. For Carrick, the writing was already on the wall.

articles.title: As actor & producer: All you need to know about Cristiano Ronaldo's first TV series, 'Day 1s', featuring former football rival Thierry Henry
articles.summary: Discover all about Cristiano Ronaldo's debut scripted TV series 'Day 1s,' featuring Thierry Henry and an all-star cast. As Ronaldo steps into a new role as producer, learn how this series aims to reshape the football drama landscape.
articles.body: Cristiano Ronaldo has spent much of his career building a global profile beyond football, but his latest project takes that ambition into a different industry. A new scripted series, developed with one of Britain's best-known film directors and featuring several familiar names from sport and entertainment, is now moving from development into production, with Ronaldo himself taking on a role behind the scenes.Ronaldo announces production of Day 1sCristiano Ronaldo has announced that production has begun on Day 1s, his first scripted television series, revealing the news in an Instagram post on Wednesday, November 11. The 41-year-old shared photographs from the London production, including one showing him alongside British filmmaker Matthew Vaughn, with whom he established the independent production company UR•Marv.“Exciting news! Production of my first TV show, Day 1s, has just started,” Ronaldo wrote. “More to come!”The announcement has brought renewed attention to a project that had been in development for several months. Ronaldo is serving as an executive producer through UR•Marv, the studio he co-founded with Vaughn, whose directing credits include the Kingsman and Kick-Ass franchises. He is also expected to appear on screen, marking his scripted acting debut after years of fronting advertising campaigns, documentaries and commercial ventures built around the CR7 brand.Ronaldo described the project as an important step beyond his playing career when the venture was first announced. “This is an exciting chapter for me, as I look ahead to new ventures,” he said.Vaughn has also explained the thinking behind their partnership. Speaking to ESPN when the studio was launched, he said: “Cristiano has created stories on the pitch that I could never have written, and I look forward to creating inspiring movies with him.”The two are also reportedly developing a separate film, Stuntnuts, about stunt performers, which is expected to star Chris Hemsworth and include a cameo from Matt Damon. Day 1s, however, is their first major television drama project.Thierry Henry, Damian Lewis and Dave join the castRonaldo is not the only football figure involved in the series. Former Arsenal and France striker Thierry Henry has also confirmed his participation, sharing photographs from the production on his own social media account. One image showed Henry seated at a desk alongside Damian Lewis, with his football shirt displayed on the wall behind them.Lewis, known for his roles in Homeland and Billions, leads the drama as Stanley Dalton, a fictional elite football agent at the centre of the story. Another production photograph showed the actor seated behind a desk, prompting jokes from fans familiar with his portrayal of billionaire Bobby Axelrod in Billions, including speculation about whether the character had turned his attention to buying a football club.British rapper Dave is also among the names attached to the production. Photographs shared from the set showed him sitting with Lewis, with a framed CR7 shirt visible behind them. Dave has previously worked as an actor, notably playing the villain Modie in the British crime drama Top Boy. The cast also includes newcomer Carlotta Banat.Filming has reportedly taken place at Barnet FC's stadium in north-west London, where Henry was photographed during production. The non-league ground has provided one of the locations for a series that appears to draw heavily on the working environment of professional football. One of the images released from the project showed a reporter inside a club dressing room, with players seated on the benches.The involvement of Henry, who represented Arsenal and Barcelona during a distinguished playing career, gives the production a prominent football presence beyond Ronaldo. The pair were rivals during their Premier League careers, but are now collaborating on a fictional account of the industry surrounding the sport.A football agent at the centre of the dramaRather than following Ronaldo or Henry as versions of themselves, Day 1s is built around the fictional Stanley Dalton, played by Lewis. The series was created by football agent Darren Dein, who is also an executive producer and represents Henry.The story is expected to explore the business and relationships behind modern British football, with the work of an influential agent providing its central narrative. That gives the drama a different starting point from a conventional football series focused primarily on players, matches or dressing-room relationships.According to a television industry source quoted by The Sun, the project could attract substantial interest from streaming platforms because of the people involved and the subject matter.“It's likely to spark a bidding war between the streamers,” the source said. “The sheer calibre of figures behind it, not to mention the cast, means it's a prestige project, albeit a surprising one for Ronaldo as he crosses into making dramas.”The source also pointed to the international interest in British football following the World Cup, particularly in the United States, where programmes such as Ted Lasso have helped introduce the sport and its culture to a wider audience.“But this isn't a sitcom. It's definitely a drama, with some comedic elements, and has some serious names backing it,” the source added.The production is therefore aiming for a different tone from the lighter football comedy that has found an audience in recent years. Its focus on agents and the business of the game could give it access to a part of professional football that is rarely explored in scripted television.Ronaldo's next chapter away from PortugalThe announcement comes during a significant period in Ronaldo's career. On November 5, he released a five-minute video message confirming his retirement from international football, bringing an end to a Portugal career that had lasted 23 years.He leaves as the country's record appearance-maker and leading goalscorer, with 234 caps and 146 goals. Ronaldo captained Portugal to its first European Championship title at Euro 2016 and also helped the national team win the UEFA Nations League in 2019 and 2025.His decision followed a reported deterioration in his relationship with Portugal manager Jorge Jesus. Ronaldo reportedly walked out of the national team's training camp without permission in late September and subsequently served a 30-day suspension. His retirement announcement came shortly before Portugal were due to name their squad for the upcoming Nations League fixtures.Although he has ended his international career, Ronaldo remains an active player at Al-Nassr in Saudi Arabia. He is currently reported to have scored 985 career goals, leaving him 15 short of the 1,000-goal milestone he has been pursuing. Stepping away from international football also removes the demands of travelling for Portugal, allowing him to concentrate on his club commitments as he approaches that target.The television project gives him another avenue to develop his interests outside the pitch while continuing his playing career. His involvement extends beyond lending his name to a production: through UR•Marv, he is taking on an executive role in the creation of scripted entertainment, with a potential acting appearance adding another dimension to the venture.For now, Ronaldo's announcement confirms that Day 1s has moved into production, with its cast and creative team assembled. A broadcaster or streaming platform, release date and further details about his own role have yet to be announced.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Football: Lamine Yamal not getting 'special privileges' playing for Spain, says Luis de la Fuente
articles.summary: Spain head coach Luis de la Fuente denies claims Lamine Yamal received "special privileges" after being allowed to join the national team later than the rest of the squad.
articles.body:
Spain head coach Luis de la Fuente has denied claims Lamine Yamal received "special privileges" after being allowed to join the national team later than the rest of the squad.

The 19-year-old did not travel with Spain for Thursday's Nations League match against the Czech Republic because of discomfort and inflammation in his right knee following Barcelona's La Liga victory over Atletico Madrid, remaining in Barcelona to work with the club's medical staff.

"I decided that, to avoid the trip, it would be better for him to stay at home and continue treatment with his club," De la Fuente said on Wednesday.

"Lamine [Yamal] doesn't have any special privileges. We would have done this for any other player.

"What hurts me most is the lying, the lack of rigour, the absence of truthfulness and the fabrication. I can't stand people who try to deceive you and lie."

Real Sociedad captain Mikel Oyarzabal is also expected to join up with the squad late while recovering from flu and having just welcome his second child.

Reports in Spanish media suggested Lamine Yamal had been given special treatment because he was not required to report to the national team immediately.

I have experienced racism a thousand times - Lamine Yamal

De la Fuente's comments come amid continued focus on Lamine Yamal's workload, with the winger playing a leading role for both Barcelona and Spain despite still being a teenager.

Lamine Yamal has played 16 times for his club this season, scoring 13 times and producing 12 assists.

He played 45 matches last season and has played 14 times for Spain in 2026.

Lamine Yamal is expected to reunite with the Spain squad before Sunday's match against England (19:45 GMT).

De la Fuente said: "The recovery is going well and we believe he will be with us on Friday."

articles.body:
A strong argument can be made that the Georgia Bulldogs are the best team in college football.

The top-ranked Bulldogs are 3-0 against Top 25 opposition. Two of those victories were blowouts in which they held their opponent under 10 points.

Georgia gets another chance to add to its resume in Week 11 at home against the Missouri Tigers.

Kirby Smart's team has two more Top 25 hurdles to clear in the next two weeks before it can feel comfortable about its spot in the top four of the College Football Playoff rankings.

Elsewhere in the SEC on Sunday, Arch Manning and the Texas Longhorns get to experience Death Valley at night in their showdown with the LSU Tigers.

The sixth-ranked Longhorns could use a win in a difficult road environment to solidify their postseason resume.

All of the weather forecasts for Week 11's top games can be found here on The Weather Channel.

Week 11 Top 25 Schedule, Odds and Weather

Northwestern at No. 20 Ohio State (-13.5)

Prediction: Ohio State 26, Northwestern 13

No. 22 Missouri at No. 1 Georgia (-15.5)

Boston College at No. 5 Notre Dame (-29.5)

Prediction: Notre Dame 37, Boston College 10

Oregon State at No. 24 Boise State (-14.5)

Prediction: Boise State 38, Oregon State 14

No. 17 South Carolina (-7.5) at Arkansas

Prediction: South Carolina 27, Arkansas 13

No. 12 Texas Tech at No. 25 Oklahoma State (-3.5)

Prediction: Oklahoma State 51, Texas Tech 45

Georgia annihilated both of its last two Top 25 opponents by a combined score of 69-15.

The Georgia football machine seems to be rolling again after a surprise loss at the hands of the Auburn Tigers on October 17.

The UGA defense found another gear in the last two weeks, as it held the Florida Gators and Ole Miss Rebels to single digits. A similar fate could await the Missouri Tigers in Athens on Saturday afternoon.

Mizzou is 1-3 against ranked foes this season. It was outscored 65-23 in its last two Top 25 games against Ole Miss and Texas, both of whom were in the top 10 at the time of those contests.

The Tigers do have a home win over the then-No. 8 Florida Gators to boast about, but that seems more like an outlier than a true representation of where they stand in the SEC hierarchy.

UGA is expected to roll at home and cover the 15.5-point spread behind its impressive defense and the steady hand of quarterback Gunner Stockton.

A win would set up a fascinating Week 12 clash on the road with the South Carolina Gamecocks, who are making a late surge toward a playoff spot.

LSU's home-field advantage is so valuable that it is a 4.5-point favorite against sixth-ranked Texas on Saturday night.

Sure, Baton Rouge at night is an incredibly difficult place to play, but LSU hasn't exactly impressed in the big spots in Lane Kiffin's first year in charge.

LSU lost Kiffin's return to Oxford in September, then fell in overtime to the Kentucky Wildcats in October and opened November with a home loss to the Alabama Crimson Tide.

Texas is on a similar level as Alabama at the moment. That has to strike up some concern in the LSU camp that Arch Manning and Co. will come into Tiger Stadium and pick up a victory.

Texas is 2-0 on the road with wins over the Tennessee Volunteers and Missouri. LSU has a better home environment than both of those teams, but it is notable that the Longhorns have picked up a pair of Top 25 victories away from home.

Additionally, Texas is 4-0 against ranked teams. LSU is 2-2 versus the Top 25 with both of those losses coming against Top 10 teams.

All of those numbers make Texas an intriguing underdog. LSU might win outright, but we shouldn't expect the Tigers to run away with the contest given Texas' resolve in most games this season.

articles.title: Expert CFB Locks, Predictions for Texas vs. LSU and Week 11 Biggest Games
articles.summary: Last week, it all felt so big on paper. Big matchups, huge outcomes. We circled the date six months ago, and it delivered.
articles.body:
Last week, it all felt so big on paper. Big matchups, huge outcomes. We circled the date six months ago, and it delivered.

This week, the buffet of games offers something different—something a bit more chaotic and unknown. It might not have the same high-profile feel, but don't let the slate of games do that.

Things are about to get very weird. And we love weird.

When it happens, we tend to do very well with our picks. When it doesn't, and it really didn't last week, we don't necessarily produce massive weeks.

With that acknowledged, we didn't post a winning week for the first time in a month. We missed a .500 week by a half-point. We didn't love what the officials did in the Missouri-Texas game, either.

On paper, we love this slate. We're just going to say it now. Hopefully, it proves to be true.

Lane Kiffin's facial expressions last week said it all.

LSU's lackluster showing against Alabama did include some positives. The Tigers tallied 457 yards of offense, while limiting Alabama to just 285 yards. Quarterback Sam Leavitt, who accounted for most of those yards, created some magical plays.

Two turnovers and an ugly fourth-down showing proved to be the difference. Sometimes, that happens. It just happened at a terrible time.

Moving forward, as long as the Tigers' hearts aren't completely broken, the team is still full of talent and potential, especially at home.

As for Texas, Arch Manning was spectacular last week against Missouri. It might have been his best collegiate game. It was refreshing to see the team let him throw the ball downfield.

The officiating certainly helped Texas, without a doubt. But the team—and the quarterback—deserve a lot of credit.

Despite what last week showed, LSU is still one of the most talented teams in college football. Texas is as well, which is what makes this such a delightful matchup.

But we like LSU, no matter what Kiffin's facial expressions told us. While the outcome against Alabama wasn't a fluke by any means, look for the Tigers to right a lot of wrongs on Saturday.

A team with legitimate playoff hopes, coming off a convincing win, is a small favorite against one of the nation's biggest disappointments, coming off yet another disappointing loss.

You know precisely where the public will be sprinting. If you read this weekly staple at all, you know we'll be cruising in the opposite direction.

Granted, we've done this with Texas A&M before. Despite the team's issues, the oddsmakers haven't lost faith. Although if you played the Aggies last week against South Carolina—a game they battled through—maybe you have.

Texas A&M was covering essentially the whole game. Until it wasn't.

As for Tennessee, the Vols delivered a suffocating win over Kentucky in Week 10. The defense was excellent once again. The offense, behind a strong running game, did enough.

With that said, the last two road games the Vols have played haven't gone great. They nearly lost to Arkansas. Then, they lost outright to South Carolina, failing to cover both times.

Will A&M burn us again? Perhaps. But we're back on them regardless.

The Utes just delivered one of the biggest wins of the season against BYU. On the other side, Arizona needed a miracle win as more than a touchdown favorite against TCU to keep its excellent season intact.

Despite a wild week of play for both teams, the oddsmakers see this game being close. We agree.

In terms of football hangovers, the potential looms large. Utah just beat its rival in a thrilling comeback.

Will that win and the celebration that ensued linger beyond last Saturday?

We've seen it plenty of times thus far. It wouldn't shock to see it again. It's worth noting that the Utes are an absurd 7-1 against the spread this season. (We fully acknowledge this excellence while still fading said excellence.)

Arizona has covered the spread only three times, although the Wildcats have played better at home. Perhaps last week's TCU performance, which needed a special-teams gaffe at the end to happen, was the ultimate lookahead spot.

Either way, the oddsmakers see this team as competitive. The defense has been solid. The offense, led by quarterback Noah Fifita, can make plays.

All of this sets up a fascinating matchup that will ultimately deliver Utah its first loss.

Latest CFB Odds, Picks Factoring in Weather

If you like points, this football game is for you.

With a total in the low 70s, each team should find success on offense. Oklahoma State is currently No. 3 in the country in scoring offense; Texas Tech, which has new life since Thomas Castellanos took over at quarterback, is No. 14 in the same category.

The last time the Red Raiders played on the road, it didn't go well. Cincinnati blasted Texas Tech, giving this group its first and only loss of the year.

Granted, Tech has flirted with more losses. But to the team's credit, they come into this game with postseason hopes still intact.

That could change this week, though Oklahoma State has had its share of issues along the way. The Pokes are one of the most explosive teams in America and still have three losses.

All three of those losses came on the road, which could explain why the oddsmakers posted the line they did. Oklahoma State is unbeaten at home, covering every game in Stillwater.

Having quarterback Drew Mestemaker has made a world of difference. Mestemaker has scored 14 touchdowns in his last three games and 32 touchdowns this season.

He could give this Texas Tech defense fits. OK State is in a position to win this one by more than a touchdown.

Minnesota only allowed UCLA to complete eight passes last week. The only issue is that those eight completions resulted in 303 passing yards.

Oh, the Gophers battled against the unbeaten Bruins; they really did. But each time the game got close, UCLA delivered a big play on cue.

We should know; we were on Minnesota last week.

After disheartening losses in consecutive weeks, the Gophers will head to Happy Valley to take on a Penn State squad with a little momentum at last. After an ugly loss to Michigan, the Nittany Lions handled Purdue and conquered Washington on the road.

Those teams aren't exactly juggernauts, although the development feels noteworthy. Quarterback Rocco Becht finally looks settled in. Running back Carson Hansen has given this team some juice.

Naturally, many will likely flock to the underdog here, given the number of points being offered. After such a difficult, emotional stretch, however, this road trip is asking a lot of a team that might be running out of energy.

The line seems to suggest Penn State is finding itself at long last. We don't disagree.

Give the Gamecocks credit for gutting out a tough win against Texas A&M, although LaNorris Sellers' ankle is worth watching. As for Arkansas, it has battled against Tennessee and Auburn over the past four games. Don't be shocked when this is tight.

The Cyclones are a different team at home. Unfortunately, they've played in Ames only once in their last four games, beating Oklahoma State. Back home, look for Iowa State to reach .500 against a team that has lost all three road games this season.

Talk about letdown spots. After beating Miami, the Irish play at home against a severely overmatched opponent before taking on SMU the following week, which suddenly feels like a very big game. Too many points. It's that simple.

A team with two wins is favored over a team fighting for bowl eligibility. Yes, Temple has lost four straight, while UAB has won two of its last three games. The Blazers, however, have lost all four road games. We expect that trend to continue.

Washington State (-8.5) vs. Colorado State

How bad is the Colorado State defense, you ask? Well, the Rams are nearly a double-digit underdog to one-win Washington State. The Cougars' schedule hasn't been exactly favorable, though this is a week to get right.

How is a team on an eight-game losing streak favored? Well, did you watch Tulane play last week. The result was so bad, the Tulane AD unleashed a blistering statement on the program. All is not well, which is good news for Rice.

articles.title: Crystal Palace sack boss Pierre Sage after 16 games
articles.summary: Crystal Palace have sacked manager Pierre Sage after 16 games in charge and the club bottom of the table.
articles.body:
Crystal Palace have sacked manager Pierre Sage after just five months in charge, with the club bottom of the Premier League.

Former Brentford and Tottenham boss Thomas Frank is in advanced talks to take over.

Sunday's 3-1 defeat by Liverpool was Palace's fourth in succession in the Premier League.

The Eagles have won just two of their opening 10 games and also have the worst defensive record in the league, conceding 24 goals.

Palace are also 21st in the 36-team Europa League table, with one win from their four matches.

In a statement, the club said that three members of Sage's coaching staff - Jamal Alioui, Damien Della Santa and Sandy Guichard - had also left the club.

Palace added: "The club thanks Pierre and his staff for their efforts during their time in South London, and wish them well for the future.

"An update on the process of appointing a new manager will be provided in due course."

Carrick and Sage sacked in first Premier League dismissals of season - reaction

Sage is the second Premier League manager to be sacked this season, after Michael Carrick was also dismissed by Manchester United on Thursday.

The 47-year-old Frenchman was appointed on a three-year contract in June after Oliver Glasner departed at the end of last season.

He previously led Lens to a second-place finish in Ligue 1 and a first French Cup triumph in their 120-year history.

However, he has been unable to replicate Glasner's success at Palace. Glasner, now manager of Nottingham Forest , led Palace to a first FA Cup title and a Europa Conference League triumph.

Palace are winless in the league since 11 October and their losing run began with a 5-0 defeat by fierce rivals Brighton .

Sage said afterwards he felt "shame" from the defeat and admitted he did not know if he would be given time to turn Palace's fortunes around.

However, there was a degree of sympathy from some behind the scenes at Selhurst Park in the immediate aftermath of that loss.

Injuries were not kind to his plans, while the absence of forward players Jean-Philippe Mateta and Ismaila Sarr - due to a mixture of fitness and personal issues related to both players' desire to leave the club - did not help.

However, three successive defeats followed, with Palace hitting the bar and having a goal ruled out in their loss to Liverpool at Selhurst Park.

Sage won five of his 16 games in all competitions.

Palace's next Premier League match is at Coventry on 21 November, after the international break.

Frank was sacked by Tottenham in February, after just under eight months in charge.

The former Brentford boss left Spurs 16th in the Premier League and five points above the relegation zone following an eight-match winless run in the league.

Palace believe Frank is the man to lead the club away from relegation trouble.

Discussions are understood to have reached the closing stages amid growing hope that a deal can be struck before the start of next week when players start trickling back from international duty.

The club have explored other options: former Everton and Nottingham Forest boss Sean Dyche and Toulouse boss Jens Berthel Askou among them.

But Frank is viewed as the overwhelming favourite to replace Sage, whose failure to instil defensive robustness to the team was a key factor in his sacking.

Danish coach Frank has been out of work since being sacked by Tottenham in February and took the decision over the summer not to take a job in the close season.

In recent weeks, it is understood Fulham have taken an interest in Frank's situation amid some uncertainty over Alvaro Arbeloa's future.

But Fulham 's results have picked up in recent weeks and Palace have made their move.

articles.title: Lamine, sin privilegios ni descanso
articles.standfirst: Sigue las directrices de recuperación marcadas para superar las molestias en la rodilla
articles.summary: Sigue las directrices de recuperación marcadas para superar las molestias en la rodilla
articles.body: Lamine Yamal no está concentrado con la selección a causa de las molestias que tiene en la rodilla, pero trabaja con el objetivo inicial de sumarse mañana viernes al combinado nacional y estar a disposición de De la Fuente para el encuentro del domingo contra Inglaterra que se disputa en el Metropolitano. El extremo catalán está estos días siguiendo los planes de recuperación marcados por los profesionales médicos y deportivos del Barcelona y de España. No tiene privilegios. Ni descanso. "Lamine tiene inflamación en la rodilla. Nuestro servicio médico lo vio y yo decidí que, para evitar este viaje, preferí que se quedara en su casa y entrenando con el club", comentó ayer jueves Luis de la Fuente en la rueda de prensa previa al encuentro de esta noche contra Chequia. "No tiene ningún privilegio. Esto lo hubiéramos hecho por cualquier otro jugador", añadió, visiblemente molesto, el seleccionador nacional. El atacante culé, de 19 años, se ha estado pasando estos días por las instalaciones de la Ciudad Deportiva del Barcelona para realizar los ejercicios y tratamientos pautados para superar cuanto antes las molestias que arrastra en la rodilla. Su deseo es estar disponible para el encuentro de España del domingo en el Metropolitano y, lógicamente, para el choque de LaLiga contra el Villarreal. La inflamación en la articulación no era muy grave y el deseo del profesional, salvo giro en su situación, es no perderse más partidos. La intención es desplazarse mañana a Madrid, y cumplir con los planes iniciales marcados. Lamine acumula muchos minutos en sus piernas. Esta temporada ya suma 20 encuentros, entre todos los torneos con el Barça (16) y la selección (4). Todos de titular y 13 los ha jugado completos. Son más de 1.600 minutos. Ante esta importante carga, todos acordaron no forzar y seguir unas pautas de recuperación, que el internacional está siguiendo. No descuida sus tratamientos, su único objetivo es competir al máximo nivel y ser un futbolista importante para Flick y De la Fuente.

articles.title: Pierre Sage: Crystal Palace sack manager with club bottom of Premier League table after 10 matches
articles.summary: Pierre Sage was appointed by Crystal Palace in the summer on a three-year contract, replacing Oliver Glasner; the former Lyon and Lens boss won just two of his 10 Premier League games in charge and the Eagles sit bottom of the table; Palace working to bring in Thomas Frank as replacement
articles.body:
Sage, appointed in June on a three-year contract to replace Oliver Glasner, leaves with Palace bottom of the Premier League table after winning just two of his 10 league matches in charge.

Palace are working on a deal to bring in Thomas Frank as his replacement. The Dane has been out of work since he was sacked as Tottenham boss in February.

An 81-word Palace statement confirmed Sage's dismissal on Thursday afternoon, which said "three members of Pierre's coaching staff - Jamal Alioui, Damien Della Santa and Sandy Guichard - have also left the club" and added, "an update on the process of appointing a new manager will be provided in due course".

Palace, who lost Sage's final match 3-1 at home to Liverpool on Sunday, have the worst defensive record of any side in the Premier League this season, having conceded 24 goals in the competition.

Sage's predecessor Glasner had presided over the most successful period in Palace's history, winning the FA Cup, UEFA Conference League and Community Shield.

However, key players from that era of success left with him in the summer - including Maxence Lacroix and Daniel Munoz - and yet the Eagles were the lowest spenders across the Premier League in the summer.

Frank emerged as the leading contender to take over at Palace following the defeat to Liverpool on Sunday. He was among a list of names the club considered in the summer before appointing Sage.

Other candidates that had been on Palace's radar include Frank Lampard , Sean Dyche , Vitor Pereira , Kim Hellberg , Vitor Matos and Tony Popovic.

Sky Sports News also revealed that Jens Berthel Askou and Ole Werne r had been under consideration.

Werner was last in charge of RB Leipzig until being sacked in June 2026, and Berthel Askou is currently in charge of Toulouse, having joined from Motherwell in the summer.

Frank had great success at Brentford during his seven-year spell between 2018 and 2025, getting the Bees into the Premier League and then establishing them as a top-flight club, reaching a ninth-place finish in 2023.

He then moved to Tottenham last season to replace Ange Postecoglou as head coach, but was sacked after less than eight months in charge with the club in 16th place, five points above the relegation zone.

Spurs only sealed survival from relegation on the final day of last season, after Igor Tudor and then Roberto De Zerbi replaced Frank as head coach.

Frank failed to win over the Tottenham faithful, with his short tenure littered with setbacks, including drinking from a coffee cup which carried the badge of rivals Arsenal.

It is a remarkable fall from grace not only for Sage, who was crowned French manager of the year last summer, but also for a Palace side that lifted their first European silverware in May.

After a 2-0 loss at Spurs in what proved to be his penultimate league match, Sage could not hold back on his assessment. "It's a disaster," he told Sky Sports . Aside from results, that could easily point to the damage caused by the departures of Daniel Munoz and Maxence Lacroix last summer and the replacements who have to emulate their quality.

Or missing Ismaila Sarr, whose injury absence following his 21-goal haul last season has been harshly felt. Or the form of Adam Wharton, who has become a shadow of his previous self in barely three months. Or that Jean-Philippe Mateta had got himself sent off 13 minutes into his second Premier League start since August.

But there are also questions to be asked regarding Palace's rationale that the head coach was a good fit for their squad in the first place.

Hinchcliffe: Sage was always up against it

Andy Hinchcliffe speaking on Sky Sports News:

"With Pierre, a three-year contract means nothing if you start the season as poorly as they have.

"Stepping in after Oliver Glasner is like David Moyes stepping in after Sir Alex Ferguson at Man Utd. It is a very difficult job to emulate - or even get close to - what the previous coach has achieved.

"I always felt he was up against it, so I'm not really surprised. With the results they've had and the fact they are bottom of the league, that's a bit more understandable than maybe Michael Carrick's situation at Man Utd.

"I can understand (why Palace would target) Thomas [Frank], given he's out of work and the incredible job he did at Brentford.

"I knew Thomas well from his work there when they were in the Championship. He's a wonderful man, a wonderful coach and knows exactly what he's doing."

articles.title: Manchester United Fires Michael Carrick as Manager amid Rumors Linking Mauricio Pochettino
articles.summary: Manchester United announced Thursday Michael Carrick has been relieved of his duties as manager.
articles.body:
Manchester United announced Thursday Michael Carrick has been relieved of his duties as manager.

USMNT coach Mauricio Pochettino is reportedly finalizing a deal to replace Carrick, according to the Associated Press' James Robson .

ESPN's Rob Dawson reported "United have informed U.S. Soccer that they intend to trigger the $10 million (£7m) release clause in Pochettino's contract with the USMNT once personal terms are agreed upon with the 54-year-old."

Carrick, 45, replaced Ruben Amorim in January on an interim basis and was appointed to the full-time gig in May after leading United to 11 wins across 16 matches, with the club finishing third on the Premier League table and earning a berth in the Champions League.

But the 2026-27 campaign has been an abject disaster. Manchester United currently sit 18th on the table with just eight points through 10 matches, a stunning run of mediocrity for the proud club.

Manchester United have had a revolving door of managers since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013, with 11 different men holding the gig as caretakers or on a full-time basis. The Red Devils haven't won a Premier League title in that time, which has also coincided with the unpopular ownership of the Glazer family (Jim Ratcliffe leading football operations was supposed to help in that regard, though the returns to this point haven't been promising).

The constant turnover at manager, paired with inconsistent approaches to roster-building and a general sense of dysfunction within the club have led to a sustained period of United finding themselves trailing far behind Premier League powers like Arsenal, Liverpool, Chelsea and Manchester City (115 charges notwithstanding) over the past two decades.

That's the context the next manager will have to shoulder as he hopes to right the ship.

articles.title: USA Withdraws Team from FIFA U-17 World Cup Over Security Concerns in Qatar and Gulf Region
articles.summary: FIFA confirmed the United States withdrew its squad from the 2026 U-17 World Cup in Qatar due to security concerns in the host country and surrounding region.
articles.body:
FIFA confirmed the United States withdrew its squad from the 2026 U-17 World Cup in Qatar due to security concerns in the host country and surrounding region.

"FIFA's security assessments remain unchanged, and no new developments affecting the security situation around the tournament have occurred," the organization said. "FIFA understands that US Soccer's decision was made in light of the existing U.S. Level 3 travel advisory.

"The safety and security of all participants and fans remains paramount. As with all FIFA tournaments and events, we are in close contact with the relevant authorities and are looking forward to the tournament kick-off in Qatar."

The U.S. State Department currently lists Qatar at Level 3, its second-highest travel advisory level, and advises Americans to "reconsider" any travel plans.

"Iranian-supported Houthis have engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure resulting in civilian casualties and severe travel disruptions," the State Department said. "The hostilities have the potential to escalate rapidly beyond that immediate area."

According to the Associated Press' Graham Dunbar , U.S. Soccer told members of the under-17 squad on Wednesday that the team won't compete in the tournament. The federation faces a possible fine of $24,000 or more from FIFA for withdrawing this late.

The U-17 World Cup will get underway on Nov. 19 and run through Dec. 13. Portugal won the event a year ago but failed to qualify for the tournament.

articles.title: FIFA Under-17 World Cup to kick off in Qatar despite US withdrawal
articles.summary: FIFA says its ‘security assessments’ for the 48-team tournament remain unchanged after US Soccer pulled out.
articles.body:
FIFA says the Under-17 World Cup in Qatar will kick off as scheduled on November 19, despite the United States’ decision to withdraw its team from the tournament.

US Soccer withdrew its national team citing safety concerns, but the sport’s global governing body, which is hosting the tournament in Qatar, confirmed on Thursday that its plans remain unchanged.

“The safety and security of all participants and fans remain paramount. As with all FIFA tournaments and events, we are in close contact with the relevant authorities and ‌‌‌‌are looking forward to the tournament kickoff in Qatar,” FIFA told Al Jazeera in a statement hours after the USA’s announcement.

“In recent months, Qatar has successfully hosted several international events,” it added.

Qatar hosted two major international tournaments in the past two weeks.

MotoGP’s Qatar Grand Prix was successfully held on 8 and the FIP Padel World Cup 2026 concluded on the same day.

With a week until the Under-17 World Cup kicks off, FIFA confirmed that its security assessments “remain unchanged” and that no new ⁠⁠⁠⁠developments affecting the security situation around the tournament have occurred.

“FIFA understands that US Soccer’s decision was made in light of the existing US ⁠⁠⁠⁠Level 3 travel advisory,” it said.

In a letter sent to players, the US Soccer Federation ⁠⁠⁠⁠said it was cancelling the team’s pre-tournament camp and its participation in the event “in light of current circumstances”, according to the Reuters news agency.

The US State Department updated its advisory for Qatar last month, urging Americans to reconsider travel because of the risk of armed conflict.

The update referred to Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, including strikes on civilian ‌‌‌‌airports and critical infrastructure.

“The well-being of our players and staff will always be our top priority,” the US federation’s letter said.

The 48-team Under-17 tournament runs from November 19 to December 13. USA had been due ⁠⁠⁠⁠to open against Montenegro on November 21 before ⁠⁠⁠⁠facing Chile and Algeria in Group J.

articles.title: El Crystal Palace echa a Pierre Sage
articles.standfirst: El club londinense anuncia la salida del técnico francés y, aunque ya suena Thomas Frank como más que posible sustituto, avisa que comunicará al nuevo técnico próximamente
articles.summary: El club londinense anuncia la salida del técnico francés y, aunque ya suena Thomas Frank como más que posible sustituto, avisa que comunicará al nuevo técnico próximamente
articles.body: Como ha hecho hace unas horas el Manchester United con Michael Carrick, el Crystal Palace ha puesto fin a la etapa de Pierre Sage como entrenador del primer equipo. El club londinense anunció este jueves la salida del técnico francés y de tres miembros de su cuerpo técnico: Jamal Alioui, Damien Della Santa y Sandy Guichard. La decisión llega después de un inicio de temporada muy por debajo de las expectativas. En la Premier League, el Palace apenas había logrado dos victorias y un empate en diez encuentros, unos números que le mantenían en una situación comprometida en la clasificación. En la Europa League, el balance tampoco había sido especialmente convincente, con un triunfo y dos empates en cuatro partidos. A través de un comunicado oficial, la entidad quiso agradecer la labor realizada por el entrenador y sus colaboradores durante su estancia en Selhurst Park. Sin embargo, los discretos resultados han terminado precipitando el cambio de rumbo. Sage había aterrizado en el club con la misión de consolidar al Palace en la zona media de la tabla y competir con garantías en Europa, pero el equipo nunca encontró continuidad ni en juego ni en resultados. El conjunto del sur de Londres ha confirmado que próximamente informará sobre el proceso para nombrar a su sustituto, mientras la dirección deportiva trabaja ya en la búsqueda de un entrenador capaz de reconducir una temporada que ha comenzado con más dudas que certezas. No parece que vayan a tardar demasiado. Thomas Frank se postula como posible sustituto tras su paso por el Tottenham.

articles.title: Gary Neville: Man Utd's treatment of Michael Carrick 'disgusting' as Mauricio Pochettino prepares to take over at Old Trafford
articles.summary: Sky Sports' Gary Neville has criticised Man Utd's treatment of Michael Carrick following his sacking; Neville warns Mauricio Pochettino must take control of recruitment to turn things around at Old Trafford
articles.body:
Neville believes United have handled the situation poorly, with Carrick taking training in Manchester while club executives met in Monaco on Wednesday and pursued Pochettino as his replacement .

Sky Sports News understands a full agreement in principle has been reached between United and Pochettino. Talks between the club and US Soccer Federation are at the paperwork and regulatory processes stage.

Neville also warned the incoming head coach that the club's problems run much deeper than the manager, insisting Pochettino must take control of recruitment and demand significant investment.

Neville believes Carrick deserved greater respect from a club he represented with distinction as a player.

The former midfielder was initially appointed in January, following Ruben Amorim's departure, and earned a permanent two-year contract after winning 12 of his 17 games to secure Champions League qualification.

But three wins in 15 matches this season have ultimately cost him his job.

Neville had questioned Carrick's appointment at the end of last season and felt the writing was on the wall after United's 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth.

"I think after the Bournemouth game I said at the time that Manchester United effectively watched Michael Carrick resign on the pitch at the end of the game with that lap around, that wave goodbye. I think he was expecting it to come at that point and they were indecisive," he said on Sky Sports News .

"They obviously felt that they might be able to get to the international break and there could be some sort of pick-up in results, but it's been a difficult two weeks. Indecision, lack of authority, just basically really poor leadership.

"In the last 24-48 hours it's been spectacularly bad to be in Monaco as an executive and an owner whilst your manager, who's a club legend, is taking training on the pitch and simultaneously approaching the US Soccer Federation to approach Mauricio Pochettino.

"It's just quite simply disgusting. That falls well below the standard of what you would expect in any other business, in any other industry. It would be constructive dismissal and you'd be getting sued.

"The optics of being in Monaco whilst the team, the staff, the people who are running the club on a day-to-day basis are in Manchester, it's just not good and it reflects badly on the leadership.

"I don't think anybody comes out of this well at all."

Neville accepts Carrick must take responsibility for the results that have left United in the relegation zone, but believes the wider circumstances surrounding his departure are symptomatic of a club that continues to make poor decisions.

Carrick's departure will make him another name on a growing list of managers who have failed to restore United to the top of English football since Sir Alex Ferguson's retirement in 2013.

Neville believes supporters have become numb to the cycle of appointments and sackings, particularly given the money spent on players and the continued failure to build a squad capable of competing.

Asked whether the club had hit a new low, he said: "I think this is a low but it just feels like you don't even get angry anymore; you don't get animated. You just feel like nothing.

"It sort of knocks you numb because we've seen it so many times. Everybody's sick of it. The fans are sick of it.

"Michael felt that he was the right man for the job. He wanted to take it and you can't blame him for that.

"But at the end of last season, similarly to when they made the decision a few years ago with Erik ten Hag, they had to make better decisions and better choices and the people who are running the club are not making good choices in the football department.

"I mean there's some off-the-pitch stuff as well that you could argue is questionable, but the on-the-pitch stuff for the last 12-13 years has been absolutely terrible.

"I think eight managers, £1.6 billion has been spent on football players and they ended up with a back four on Sunday of [Patrick] Dorgu, [Noussair] Mazraoui, [Leny] Yoro and [Ayden] Heaven and you've spent £1.6 billion on players.

"That's very difficult to do. You could put every single one of those Manchester United fans in charge of that club or put them in the dugout and you wouldn't end up with that back four if they were running the club.

"And Michael's demise in the end is because obviously he's not been able to get the same tune out of the players. That's the accountability he has to carry as a manager.

"But when you sign those midfield players in the summer that are well below the standard of the other midfield players that have gone to other clubs. United were at the bottom of the queue when midfield players were being handed out.

"They needed midfield players; they needed to bolster that department and they ended up with players ultimately that weren't wanted by Tottenham, by [Manchester] City and others.

"And then the back four needed strengthening. That back four, five, six that are playing currently have been there for five, six years, seven years, and they've been failing for four, five, six, seven years.

"Some of them have injury problems as well and some of them are getting on. The likes of Luke Shaw, [Matthijs] De Ligt, [Lisandrp] Martinez are injured quite regularly.

"They're inconsistent when they play, and then the rest of the players who are fit, to be fair, don't meet the standards.

"So this is not unsurprising totally. I am shocked it's come this early in the season. I didn't think it would happen this quickly and I thought Manchester United would have a half-decent season, but it's come a lot quicker than anybody thought and it seems to be something that happens quite regularly at the club and it's really disappointing."

Pochettino has been considered for the United job on previous occasions, but Neville has warned him against believing that a change of manager alone will solve the club's problems.

Neville remembers visiting Pochettino at Tottenham during his early days in charge, when the Argentine was already identifying which players he wanted to build around and which he needed to move on.

"I think the mistake that Mauricio could make if he comes in is that he may get an initial bounce out of them. He may get six months of bounce out of them," Neville continued.

"I actually remember going to see him at Tottenham in his very early days. We used to, when I was coaching with England, train at Tottenham's training ground.

"He set out very quickly within the first six to eight months in the job. He had a whiteboard in front of him in his office with all the players' names on little markers and he actually moved a group of players over to the left-hand side of the board and said: 'These are the ones I know I need to get rid of. These are the ones I know I can work with and build around.'

"He's got to identify that very quickly at United and I'm sure he will do that. He's more experienced now than he was when he was at Tottenham.

"But he's got a big job to do in exiting players. Manchester United have been really poor at exiting players over the last 10 years. They've not done it very well at all."

'Pochettino needs control over recruitment,' says Neville

Neville believes Pochettino must also ensure he has sufficient financial backing and, crucially, control over recruitment.

United's summer business has done little to convince him that the existing structure can deliver the players required, and he believes the new head coach must make strong demands before taking the job.

"I'm hoping Mauricio Pochettino has done a couple of things on the way in and I'm hoping he protects himself on his contract because he'll need to.

"I'm sure he's stated that he needs a massive budget. I think he needs defenders straight away to get Manchester United anywhere near where they want to be this season.

"And the other thing is to make sure that he takes control of the recruitment because it's quite clear that what happened in the summer is well below the standard again.

"He's got to come in here and protect himself against actually the people that he's working with. They are currently trying to employ him.

"He needs to make sure he takes the club into his own hands, into his own destiny, make sure he controls his own outcomes and make sure he's absolutely unequivocal in getting money to improve the defence initially in January and improving the midfield and forward line next summer."

Neville's admiration for Pochettino - but is he the right appointment?

Neville has made no secret of his admiration for Pochettino and believes the Argentine has the coaching ability and personality to manage a club of United's stature.

But he has also seen too many different types of manager fail at Old Trafford to believe the challenge will be straightforward.

David Moyes, Louis van Gaal, Jose Mourinho, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, Erik ten Hag, Ruben Amorim and Carrick have all experienced the difficulties of the job, while Ralf Rangnick also failed to turn things around.

For Neville, that history should serve as a warning to Pochettino.

"I can't believe Mauricio would have looked at the last 13 years, looked at managers like David Moyes, Jose Mourinho and Louis van Gaal who are very experienced, brilliant operators in what they do and seen them fall short.

"He's then seen talented managers from Europe like Amorim and Ten Hag fall short.

"He's seen club legends who have got a lot of love for the club, who understand the values, understand how to play for Manchester United, understand what the fans want and can communicate that. He's seen those guys fail.

"He's seen Ralf Rangnick come in, who's got more of a sporting director background and a business background, come in and fail and tell the club they need open-heart surgery.

"So he's seen every type of manager fail at this football club over the last 13 years.

"He's got to come in and basically wipe the slate clean and start from scratch and imagine that this football club is a blank canvas because everybody that's been there in that period has been part of the failure."

Despite those concerns, Neville has consistently backed Pochettino as a candidate for the job and believes he has the qualities to succeed.

"I've always wanted Mauricio Pochettino as the manager at United. I've said it numerous times that I wanted him.

"I think he's a brilliant person. I think he'll handle the media. I think he understands the size of the club.

"But it's a monumental task to win everybody else over and get everybody on side and make sure he has a team that can compete.

"He's a brilliant coach with great experience and he's a good man.

"He also believes in young players and bringing players through and developing them and coaching them, which is what he's going to have to do at Manchester United.

"I've always liked Mauricio Pochettino. Whether this is the right point for him to take the Manchester United job, who knows? We'll find out in the next year or two.

"But I'm hoping that he's made some pretty strong demands on the way in and that he's got control of the club."

'You're probably looking at about 10 players to be sold'

For Neville, United need a complete defensive overhaul, further midfield reinforcements and a new centre-forward, with only Kobbie Mainoo currently convincing him in midfield, in a reflection of the rebuild that the incoming boss faces.

He estimates that Pochettino could need around 10 new players to get United back to where they want to be.

"If I said that the midfield that I've seen this season, only Kobbie Mainoo to me looks like he's good enough," said Neville.

"The back line, I think it needs a complete rebuild and I think we need a centre-forward.

"So I don't know how many that is and probably you could argue we need back-up in goal as well.

"So my view would be probably, I don't know yet, there's probably five or six in defence, there's two or three in midfield, there's a goalkeeper and there's probably a centre-forward.

"And I think you're probably looking at about 10 players that you would need to basically rotate out.

"Lisandro Martinez told us that basically the sporting director should have brought more players in the summer, so the players know it themselves.

"So Mauricio Pochettino, who's been around the block and knows how to manage football clubs, he'll have a pretty good idea, having watched Manchester United many times over many years.

articles.title: Andy Robertson: Scotland captain on reaching Sir Kenny Dalglish's caps record - 'He'll always be the greatest'
articles.summary: The 32-year-old will equal Dalglish's 102 caps against North Macedonia on Friday night; he will become Scotland's record cap holder if he plays the final Nations League game away to Switzerland on Monday; Scotland have won one of four games under new head coach Sebastien Pocognoli
articles.body:
It is 40 years since Dalglish won his 102nd and final Scotland cap in a 3-0 win over Luxembourg at Hampden Park, and on Friday Robertson will equal that number against North Macedonia.

The 32-year-old will then surpass that record on Monday if he plays in the final Nations League game against Switzerland in St Gallen.

"In terms of number, I'll stand side by side by him but I don't want to forget and I don't want people to forget how important this man has been for our country," Robertson said when asked about matching the 75-year-old's record.

"For me, he was arguably the best player in the world at his time and he'll always be the greatest in this country, no matter what happens in the future.

"He'll always be the first one to do X, Y and Z and that shouldn't be forgotten.

"We're not always the best at maybe remembering these great people and I think tomorrow is definitely a reason to do that for Kenny.

"Unbelievably proud, but tomorrow's not really about me, it's about him in my opinion, for how long the record stood for starters, for what he achieved in his career, for the person he is."

Robertson struck up a relationship with Dalglish when he signed for Liverpool from Hull City in 2017.

"We've had a lot of jokes [about beating his record], but I know deep down how proud he is of me and how happy he is for me as well.

"I always remember when I got the captaincy, he was one of the first to text me and say 'I know I've been out the game a little bit, but if you need help I can be that person' and to have someone like that to bounce anything off and rely on [is great].

"Him and his family have been such a massive help to my family, especially in my time at Liverpool, and I've got no doubt there will be a couple of texts that'll be exchanged.

The time when I do go above him, I'll be above him in caps only and that's where it ends.

"For me, he'll always be the greatest of this country because of what he did, how he did it and also the man he's become.

"We've had so many great players for Scotland, but for me Kenny will always stand on top and I don't think that will change."

articles.title: CFP Bracket Predictions After Latest 2026 Playoff Bowl Rankings Projections
articles.summary: The 2026 college football season is far from finished, but the playoff picture is beginning to come into focus. The College Football Playoff (CFP) selection committee released its updated rankings on Tuesday.
articles.body:
The 2026 college football season is far from finished, but the playoff picture is beginning to come into focus. The College Football Playoff (CFP) selection committee released its updated rankings on Tuesday.

The biggest issue with the rankings right now is that they're unlikely to stay static. We've seen upsets involving the top teams almost weekly. Teams ranked No. 1 in the polls have gone just 5-4 this season.

We saw another big "upset" this past week, as Notre Dame knocked off top-ranked Miami, though the Hurricanes were without Malachi Toney and the Irish were actually favored.

Here's a look at the latest rankings, what's in store for Week 11, and some early CFP bracket predictions.

The Bulldogs are the new top-ranked team in the country, not long after a surprising loss to Auburn knocked them out of the top spot. If Gunner Stockon and Co. hope to retain the No. 1 spot this time around, they'll have to fend off a scrappy Missouri team that has the goods to pull off yet another upset.

It's still hard to know what to make of this Texas team. Quarterback Arch Manning has been up-and-down all season, and we've seen the Longhorns stumble against the likes of Oklahoma, Florida, and even Ohio State—though Texas did survive the Buckeyes.

A convincing win against an LSU squad that was just squashed by Alabama would go a long way toward legitimizing the Longhorns.

USC has been a weird team this season. It played brilliantly against the Buckeyes a couple of weeks ago but looked lost in games against Oregon and Wisconsin. The Trojans need a win here to stay alive in a Big Ten race that is led by undefeated UCLA. They might get it against an Indiana team that has also looked inconsistent this season.

Utah remains undefeated and will need to beat a talented Big-12 rival this week to stay that way. Quarterback Noah Fifita and the Arizona offense are potent enough to make this one very interesting. The Utes could lose and still end up winning the conference, but they're unlikely to earn a first-round bye without a perfect record.

The CFP format will be very similar to last year's. The top four Power Four conference champions will earn automatic bids—though, they won't automatically earn top seeds as they did a couple of years ago.

This is why we could see two teams from the same conference earn first-round byes. The prediction here is that we do, with both Georgia and Alabama taking the opening round off.

A fifth guaranteed spot will go to the highest-ranked conference champion from the rest of the Group of Six. The prediction here is that Boise State earns that bid as the Pac-12 champion.

Whichever team earns the G6 bid is likely to push out a team like Texas Tech, which is currently in the No. 12 spot.

The big change this year is that Notre Dame, which doesn't exist within a conference, can earn an automatic bid by finishing inside the top 12. That would prevent the Irish from being dropped out for a team like Boise State if they end up in the No. 12 spot.

The prediction here is that Notre Dame doesn't come close to needing the automatic qualifier. The Irish survived Miami, and their remaining schedule—Boston College, SMU, at Syracuse—isn't particularly daunting.

We may not find out how good Notre Dame actually is until the playoff, but it shouldn't fall out of the CFP picture. The prediction here is that the Irish earn a high seed but are kept away from a bye by the CFP committee.

articles.title: Dan Hicks Dies at 64, Wife Hannah Storm and NBC Sports Release Statements on Legendary Sportscaster
articles.summary: Longtime NBC Sports broadcaster Dan Hicks has died at the age of 64.
articles.body:
Longtime NBC Sports broadcaster Dan Hicks has died at the age of 64.

SportsCenter anchor Hannah Storm, who married Hicks in 1994, issued a statement Thursday announcing her husband died "following an acute illness."

NBC Sports also issued a statement about Hicks' contributions to the network over the past 34 years.

ESPN chairman Jimmy Pitaro released a statement about Hicks on behalf of the network.

Born in Tucson, Hicks graduated from the University of Arizona in 1984 with a bachelor's degree in journalism.

Hicks became a national sports anchor for CNN in 1989 after working for local radio and television affiliates in the Tucson area. He spent three years with the network before joining NBC Sports in the summer of 1992.

Hicks was part of NBC's coverage for many of its biggest sporting events, including 16 Olympics between the Summer and Winter Games. He received a Sports Emmy in the 2024 Paris Olympics, which was honored in the Outstanding Live Special – Championship Event category as part of NBC's coverage for the 2024 Summer Olympics

articles.title: La Liga que gana el Rayo y en la que el Real Madrid acaba undécimo
articles.standfirst: El club de Vallecas lidera el índice de PLAIER y la Universidad de St. Gallen. Tiene la mejor puntuación financiera de Primera y supera a Villarreal y Getafe en la valoración global, pese a que ambos sacan una A en el banquillo
articles.summary: El club de Vallecas lidera el índice de PLAIER y la Universidad de St. Gallen. Tiene la mejor puntuación financiera de Primera y supera a Villarreal y Getafe en la valoración global, pese a que ambos sacan una A en el banquillo
articles.body: El Getafe tiene el banquillo más eficiente de Primera, el Elche saca la mejor nota en la confección de la plantilla y el Rayo Vallecano gana en la suma. El club de Vallecas es el único de LaLiga que obtiene una B en la evaluación global del Global State of Football 2025-26, el informe de PLAIER y la Universidad de St. Gallen que analiza a 248 clubes de 14 ligas. Su ventaja se entiende al mirar las tres notas por separado: el Rayo puntúa en positivo en las cuentas, en la confección de la plantilla y en el rendimiento del banquillo. Ni el Villarreal ni el Getafe, sus dos perseguidores, lo consiguen. La mayor ventaja del Rayo sobre el Villarreal está en las cuentas. El club de Vallecas obtiene +0,40 y una B en estabilidad financiera, la mejor puntuación de Primera en ese apartado, por delante del +0,39 del Real Madrid. El Villarreal se queda en −0,61 y una D, y el Getafe, en −0,37 y otra D. El estudio valora la relación entre el gasto de personal y los ingresos, el margen de beneficio y el peso del patrimonio neto en el balance. La posición del Rayo refleja cómo se sostienen sus cuentas en relación con sus recursos. El Villarreal compensa parte de esa distancia desde el banquillo. Su cuerpo técnico obtiene un +1,16, por el +0,44 del Rayo, al medir el rendimiento en función de la calidad estimada de cada plantilla. El equipo de Vallecas recupera terreno en la confección del grupo: suma +0,25 frente al −0,11 del Villarreal. En ese apartado, el informe compara la calidad de los jugadores con la que cabría esperar de un club con un gasto de personal similar en la misma liga. El balance deja al Rayo primero con +0,47 y al Villarreal segundo con +0,21 en el índice global. El Getafe firma la mejor nota de Primera en el banquillo, un +1,87 y una A. Al mismo tiempo, obtiene un −2,17 y una F en la confección de la plantilla. Las dos calificaciones parten de preguntas distintas. La primera mide cuánto rindió el equipo con los jugadores que tenía. La segunda, qué calidad de plantilla consiguió reunir con su presupuesto estimado. Según el modelo, el Getafe sacó mucho rendimiento de un grupo cuya calidad se quedó por debajo de lo esperable para su nivel de gasto. En la evaluación global termina tercero, con +0,15. El Rayo supera al Getafe en cuentas y en confección de plantilla, y al Villarreal en esos mismos dos apartados. A eso añade una B en el banquillo. Ahí está la explicación de su primer puesto: los dos equipos que más se le acercan le ganan en rendimiento del cuerpo técnico, pero Vallecas les saca ventaja en cómo sostiene sus cuentas y en la plantilla que consigue reunir con sus recursos. El Elche, quinto en el índice español, es el único equipo de Primera con una A en eficiencia de la dirección deportiva. El Real Madrid, undécimo en la general, roza el liderato financiero. El informe señala que destinó menos de la mitad de sus ingresos a gastos de personal y que la facturación creció con las nuevas vías de ingresos del Bernabéu renovado, mientras esa partida se mantuvo prácticamente estable. El Barcelona, sexto, obtiene una B en rendimiento del banquillo y dos D, en estabilidad financiera y confección de plantilla. El Atlético es decimoquinto y recibe una F en este último apartado. Sevilla y Levante cierran la clasificación española y son los únicos con una F en estabilidad financiera.

articles.title: Mauricio Pochettino will coach USMNT vs. Haiti despite looming Manchester United move
articles.summary: The U.S. coach hasn't addressed his future with players, but they're already considering what his departure would mean for a team that credits him with raisi...
articles.body:
FAYETTEVILLE, Ga. — Mauricio Pochettino was back at work with the U.S. on Thursday, preparing his squad for a match against Haiti on Saturday. But with Manchester United's announcement that Michael Carrick had been dismissed as manager, the Argentine's days leading the Americans appear to be winding down.

Pochettino will coach the U.S. through both legs of the CONCACAF Nations League quarterfinals against Haiti, even if his departure is announced before Tuesday's second leg in Cincinnati, sources confirmed to Yahoo Sports.

The U.S. Soccer Federation has spoken to United about releasing Pochettino from his contract and freeing him to become the Red Devils' leader, sources told Yahoo Sports.

U.S. players are bracing for that eventuality, even as they continue preparing for the CONCACAF Nations League quarterfinals.

"I expect official news soon," a person close to the situation said.

"Him leaving, him staying, he's just created a great foundation and a great base for this team," midfielder Sebastian Berhalter said of the 54-year-old Pochettino. "Even though he's an Argentinian coach, he made us even more proud to be American, and I think that speaks volumes of who he is as a person and as a coach."

Berhalter said Pochettino has not addressed the United situation with the players.

Pochettino is not scheduled to speak publicly until Friday morning — standard procedure the day before a game. The USSF has not commented on the situation.

"If I had a vote, I would like to keep things the way they are," striker Folarin Balogun said. "Things have been working well. We have a clear sense of identity. We have a clear playing style, and whenever you have a top coach, you want them to stay."

Pochettino joined the U.S. program in the fall of 2024 following Gregg Berhalter's dismissal and, after guiding the team to the World Cup's Round of 16 this past summer, he re-signed with the USSF through the 2030 tournament. His deal included an exit clause of a reported $10 million, which United would need to pay the USSF.

Sebastian Berhalter, who has become a key figure for the U.S., credited Pochettino for his rise on the international scene, inviting him to his first camp in the summer of 2025.

"From Day 1, he's always believed in me," the 25-year-old midfielder said. "I can't thank him enough, regardless if he's the coach, not the coach. He's meant so much to me, and he's helped me develop as a player and as a person."

With Pochettino seemingly on the way out, Balogun reflected on where the program stands.

"The benefit and the blessing when you have a great coach is the standard," he said. "Coach has definitely raised the standard since he's been in charge. Just the intensity of training, how we approach games. He's changed our way of thinking as players."

This is not the first time U.S. players have had to compartmentalize their work while rumors swirled around Pochettino, whose experience with Tottenham Hotspur, Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea, among others, has made him a prime candidate for openings abroad.

During the long run-up to the World Cup, both Tottenham and AC Milan were reportedly interested in him.

"We already deal with a lot of other things, and this doesn't change what we do on the field," Berhalter said. "We know what we're supposed to do, and I think the work ethic, the fighting mentality, that spirit, isn't going to change regardless."

The U.S. is scheduled to practice again Friday at the national training center before chartering to Miami.

Right back Sergiño Dest is departing camp with an undisclosed injury he brought with him from PSV Eindhoven, the USSF said. He had been under evaluation this week. No replacement will be named at this late date in camp.

articles.title: Owono pide hablar con la familia de Jesús de Miguel
articles.standfirst: El portero del Andorra sigue 'encerrado' en casa y ha planteado al club la opción de comunicarse con el entorno del fallecido cuando crean oportuno
articles.summary: El portero del Andorra sigue 'encerrado' en casa y ha planteado al club la opción de comunicarse con el entorno del fallecido cuando crean oportuno
articles.body: Owono sigue muy tocado. Casi sin salir de casa y en tratamiento. El portero se ha puesto en manos de los psicólogos y doctores del club y, poco a poco, se va sintiendo con más fuerzas, pero lejos de recuperar algo de normalidad. De hecho, aún no ha regresado a los entrenamientos ni lo hará hasta que no esté preparado. Eso sí, el portero del Andorra ha pedido al club que intente generar un encuentro, por carta, por teléfono o viajando a Toledo, con la familia de Jesús de Miguel para compartir con ellos el dolor que sienten y darles el pésame en primera persona. El portero ya quiso llamar a la familia el día después del accidente e incluso compartió con los suyos la posibilidad de acudir al sepelio, pero desde el Andorra y desde su gente más cercana le recomendaron dejar pasar más tiempo. El jugador ha pedido nuevamente intentar hablar con los familiares y ponerse a su disposición. Esta vez en Andorra se ha puesto en contacto con el Tenerife para hablar de esta situación y desde el club isleño le han pedido algo más de tiempo para "respetar el duelo de la familia". Por tanto, de momento hay que esperar mientras la familia recupera la compostura en la medida en la que le sea posible y Owono sale de un pozo complicado de abandonar y sin saber si volverá a entrenarse o a jugar con sus compañeros. La situación del portero del Andorra sigue siendo complicada. Piqué sigue estando al pie del cañón y sus visitas al chico son constantes. Su madre y su pareja sigue estando en casa para acompañarle en este momento tan complicado y sus compañeros realizan visitas casi a diario para ver cómo se encuentra. Tanto Tenerife como Andorra están tratando la situación con especial tacto y delicadeza y dando ejemplo de ser dos clubes con mucho sentido común. "Hay que darle espacio para que se sienta totalmente libre de tomar cualquier decisión, de querer volver o no, cuando lo considere oportuno y esté preparado", comentaba el entrenador del andorra Carles Manso en la previa del regreso del equipo del Principado a la competición liguera. El club ha puesto a disposición de toda la plantilla en sesiones grupales o individuales la ayuda de psicólogos para que los jugadores puedan superar la situación. También se ha puesto en marcha el respaldo de la AFE, que en silencio no olvida la situación de Owono, sus compañeros y, obviamente, la plantilla del Tenerife.
