articles.summary: El XXX Torneo Internacional se disputará en el estadio de Gran Canaria los días 27, 28 y 29 de diciembre y contará con la presencia del Tenerife
articles.body: El XXX Torneo Internacional LaLiga FC Futures, que se disputará en el estadio de Gran Canaria los días 27, 28 y 29 de diciembre, homenajeará a Jesús de Miguel. El torneo contará con la presencia del Tenerife, según desveló José Ramón De la Morena este miércoles, entre los 16 equipos integrantes del torneo, y sus jugadores llevarán el nombre del futbolista fallecido el pasado 3 de noviembre. "Hemos querido tener un guiño, un detalle. Este año no solo jugará la UD Las Palmas sino que también jugará el Tenerife. Le vamos a ascender también a primera división estas navidades en memoria de Jesús de Miguel. Hemos invitado al Tenerife y los niños del Tenerife lucirán en su espalda el nombre de Jesús de Miguel", anunció De la Morena en la presentación del torneo. El torneo, organizado por LaLiga y la Fundación José Ramón De la Morena, cumplirá en esta edición 30 años, 25 de los cuales se han disputado en Canarias. Por segunda edición consecutiva, se disputará en el estadio de la UD Las Palmas, un escenario en el que los niños se sentirán más cerca todavía de poder imitar a sus ídolos. 16 equipos tratarán de ganar el título, 11 españoles y cinco internacionales. La lista de candidatos la componen Sevilla, Juventus, Barcelona, Espanyol, Real Madrid, Atlético, Bayer Leverkusen, Betis, Inter, Borussia Dortmund, Elche, Villarreal, Las Palmas, Paris Saint-Germain, Getafe y Tenerife. El Atlético, ganador en la XXIX edición, defenderá título.

articles.title: La FIFA ya conoce la candidatura del Bernabéu a la final del Mundial 2030
articles.standfirst: El equipo de inspección ha pasado hoy por el templo madrididista
articles.summary: El equipo de inspección ha pasado hoy por el templo madrididista
articles.body: Madrid se asoma al Mundial 2030. El equipo de inspección de FIFA ya está en la capital y el Santiago Bernabéu ha sido este jueves el gran escaparate de una candidatura que quiere jugar un papel protagonista en 2030. La delegación del organismo internacional, acompañada por responsables de la Real Federación Española de Fútbol, ha continuado en Madrid el recorrido técnico que está realizando por las sedes españolas aspirantes a albergar partidos de la Copa del Mundo. La visita forma parte del proceso de evaluación de las ciudades y estadios que integrarán el proyecto mundialista de España, Portugal y Marruecos. Tras su paso por Barcelona, donde examinó el Camp Nou y el RCDE Stadium, y por Zaragoza, con parada en la futura Nueva Romareda, el turno llegó a una ciudad llamada a convertirse en uno de los grandes epicentros del torneo. El punto neurálgico de la jornada fue el Santiago Bernabéu, un estadio que por capacidad, historia, ubicación y modernización aparece como uno de los recintos de referencia dentro de todo el proyecto del Mundial 2030 y candidato a albergar la final. Allí se desarrolló una intensa sesión de trabajo en la que participaron representantes de FIFA, técnicos de la RFEF, responsables del Real Madrid y miembros de las distintas administraciones implicadas en la organización del torneo. Madrid presentó ante los inspectores internacionales buena parte de sus credenciales. No sólo la transformación integral del Bernabéu, convertido en uno de los recintos más avanzados del mundo, sino también la capacidad hotelera de la ciudad, sus infraestructuras de transporte, la red de comunicaciones y la experiencia acumulada en la organización de grandes acontecimientos deportivos y culturales. A la reunión acudieron representantes del Ayuntamiento de Madrid, de la Comunidad de Madrid y del Gobierno de España, reflejando el carácter estratégico que tiene para todas las instituciones la organización de un Mundial que regresaría al fútbol español 48 años después de la edición de 1982. La inspección de FIFA busca comprobar sobre el terreno aspectos clave para la celebración del torneo, desde los accesos a los estadios hasta los planes de movilidad, seguridad, sostenibilidad y atención a aficionados. Son visitas exhaustivas en las que se analizan cientos de detalles que terminarán definiendo el mapa definitivo de sedes mundialistas. Para Madrid, la candidatura supone mucho más que albergar varios partidos. La capital aspira a convertirse en una de las imágenes icónicas del Mundial 2030, apoyada en un Bernabéu que ya mira al futuro y en una ciudad acostumbrada a recibir grandes eventos internacionales. El examen continúa, pero la sensación en el entorno de la candidatura es que Madrid juega sus cartas desde una posición privilegiada dentro del proyecto que llevará el centenario de la Copa del Mundo a tres continentes.

articles.title: Giuliano, el trabajo extra… da sus frutos
articles.standfirst: Lleva toda la temporada añadiendo, al menos una vez a la semana, una sesión individual para pulir sus carencias. Sus números le avalan: son los mejores desde que llegó al Atlético
articles.summary: Lleva toda la temporada añadiendo, al menos una vez a la semana, una sesión individual para pulir sus carencias. Sus números le avalan: son los mejores desde que llegó al Atlético
articles.body: “Yo soy muy transparente y sincero. Creo que técnicamente tengo que mejorar mucho. Tengo que mejorar en los metros finales, tener más pausa, más tranquilidad. Obviamente en el día a día, en los entrenamientos, intento mejorar, siempre en tomarme un tiempo más, una pausa más”. Aquí, Giuliano Simeone. Aquí, el jugador del Atlético confesando su deseo de seguir creciendo en las páginas de MARCA hace algo más de un año. A fe que ha puesto todo de su parte para lograrlo. Por eso, el 20 rojiblanco tiene trabajo extra, que consiste en al menos una vez a la semana añadir sesiones individuales a los entrenamientos del equipo. Trabajo consensuado con el cuerpo técnico para pulir esas carencias que nadie mejor que él, competitivo como marca su apellido, sabe que tiene. Un trabajo extra, en definitiva, que busca seguir creciendo a la velocidad que lleva haciéndolo desde que hace más de dos años se instaló en el primer equipo rojiblanco. Dos cesiones a Zaragoza y Alavés le valieron el billete de vuelta al club de su vida, el mismo en el que escaló en su cantera hasta la élite. Todo, claro, con trabajo y un afán de superación que le sirvió para superar con nota una lesión grave cuando estaba a préstamo en Vitoria. El argentino, concentrado con su selección en este parón, ha ido mejorando sus números desde que forma parte de la primera plantilla. Así, sus 4 goles y 2 asistencias en los 16 partidos de esta temporada están ya cerca de los 5 que firmó en la 24-25. Por progresión, debería superar los 7 con los que cerró el pasado curso, demostrando que ese trabajo individual le está haciendo pulir las carencias. Su gol a un toque ante el Barça demuestra que va creciendo y que los choques ante los grandes rivales le motivan como al que más. Tanto que los de los azulgranas y los del Real Madrid son los partidos donde más genera: 5 goles/asistencias en los derbis por 3 en los choques ante los catalanes para un jugador que es el segundo máximo asistente del equipo, 19 por 20 de Julián, desde que llegó… y el cuarto máximo goleador del equipo (16), por detrás de Julián (51), Sorloth (44) y Griezmann (31) desde que forma parte del primer equipo.

articles.title: Mauricio Pochettino to Manchester United: How United's pursuit of former Tottenham and Chelsea manager unfolded
articles.summary: Manchester United have sacked Michael Carrick with Mauricio Pochettino set to succeed him at Old Trafford; Rob Dorsett has the full story behind the sacking and how the move for Pochettino gathered momentum and whether Unai Emery was truly ever in the running
articles.body:
However, the decision was taken in 2024 that the timing wasn't right for either side.

United are close to completing a deal for the Argentine to take over from Michael Carrick in time for the Premier League game against Liverpool at Anfield a week on Sunday.

Pochettino is a coach who has long been admired at Old Trafford. Before the INEOS takeover, he was considered for the role by the previous regime, who ultimately decided to go with Ten Hag instead.

The meeting in the summer of 2024 took place shortly after Omar Berrada became United's chief executive. Ten Hag was sacked in the October. Pochettino was out of work having left Chelsea in May.

It's thought that, while Pochettino was seen as a brilliant man-manager and a sound tactician, United's bosses felt he had been emotionally bruised by the latter stages of his time at Stamford Bridge and with some complex relationships and a rebuilding job to be done within the Manchester United squad, the timing didn't feel right.

However, once United were told a few weeks ago about Pochettino's £7.4m buy-out clause in his US contract, and after they had been given positive signals from the Pochettino camp about his desire to take charge at Old Trafford, Berrada and Jason Wilcox, the director of football, decided the timing was right.

Their first direct contact with Pochettino, Sky Sports News understands, was on Tuesday night, around the same time that there was an official approach to his employers, the United States Soccer Federation (USSF).

Sky Sports News has also been told the United hierarchy at this stage went fully behind their pursuit of Pochettino, once it became clear last week that Unai Emery could not be prised out of Aston Villa.

Both coaches, we have been told, fit United's demand for a boss that can cope with the size of the club, and protect the players from the outside 'noise'. The club's bosses were determined that was the biggest problem for the first head coach employed in the INEOS era, Ruben Amorim.

Berrada and Wilcox have been huge admirers of Emery for some time, and he was very high on their list of possible candidates if and when they decided to sack Carrick.

It was an avenue United were keen to progress, if they could see a way of making it work. However, after detailed discussions with intermediaries, it soon became clear that Emery had a watertight contract at Villa Park with no buy-out clause, which made it impossible for United to progress. There were never any direct discussions with Emery or Villa, and Villa's bosses had made it very clear they are not prepared to allow him to leave.

Sources close to the club have stressed there is no suggestion Pochettino is second choice, and rather - on the recommendation of Berrada and Wilcox - co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe is satisfied that he is the best man for the job. There were no direct discussions with Julian Nagelsmann, Eddie Howe or Antonio Conte.

United bosses hurt by criticism of their treatment of Carrick

It's understood that United's bosses are hurt by suggestions that they have treated Carrick badly, allowing him to continue to take training while they were progressing a deal for Pochettino in the background.

They are adamant that nobody within the club leaked information about the talks with the Argentinian coach and their priority throughout has been to treat Carrick with the respect due to a true legend of the club.

Equally, until they had full agreement with Pochettino, they were reluctant to relieve Carrick of his duties, for fear of being left in limbo with no head coach in post.

The board were adamant that Carrick had to be told face-to-face, and so once they had returned from their review with Ratcliffe in Monaco on Wednesday night, they called a meeting with Carrick for 8.30am Thursday to deliver the news. We are told Carrick was upset by the decision, but understood the reasons.

Back in January when he was first given the interim role, United's bosses didn't have a definite plan to continue with Carrick in a substantive role, beyond the end of the season. But they were impressed by his integrity and his innate understanding of the club, his vital work with the academy, the incredibly positive impact he and his staff had on the squad and also by the results, which secured a third-placed Premier League finish and a Champions League spot.

That exceeded the board's expectations, and there was a real desire at that stage for him to succeed going forward.

Nevertheless, before giving Carrick a two-year contract, Wilcox and Berrada carried out a full round of due diligence and spoke to a number of other possible candidates in the new year. But because of the success Carrick had achieved, because of the positivity within the squad, and because of the huge groundswell of support from the United fans, the hierarchy felt they had no choice but to continue with him in the head coach role.

He was given a two-year, and not a longer, contract with minimal costs to either party should there be a termination.

Results and mood have been very different this season, and the feeling was Carrick's position became increasingly untenable.

After the heavy defeats to Bournemouth and Como last month, United's football bosses decided there needed to be a full review at the start of the international break. Despite the comeback win against Roma and the comeback draw against Villa, the feeling was that performances and the structure within the team had become chaotic, and so the decision was taken to propose a change to Ratcliffe.

The overriding feeling was that a "bubble of negativity" had descended on the squad, as evidenced by the on-pitch performances, and the off-pitch public criticisms from Lisandro Martinez and captain Bruno Fernandes.

While Carrick had overseen results that exceeded expectations last season, the feeling was that the team was grossly underachieving now, with one win in 11 matches and a descent into the relegation places. That was deemed unacceptable, for a squad which the board felt was worthy of being top-six in the Premier League.

There seems to be some sympathy for Carrick concerning the injuries which have depleted his squad this season, and it is likely that is something United will address in January, as they look to back Pochettino in the early stages of his reign.

Originally endorsed by Sir Alex Ferguson - a fact not inconsequential despite the Scot's retirement some 13 years ago - Pochettino holds clout among football's elite. At nearly every turn of the post-Ferguson era, United have failed to appoint a leader of stature and appropriate experience, perhaps with Mourinho the only exception.

Pochettino is a personality. On top of his attractive brand of football and a commitment to player pathways, he has proved he can handle himself under pressure, not least in his most recent role as US national head coach, at a home World Cup, where his team's campaign was overshadowed, in his own words, by "politics and manipulation".

articles.title: República Checa - España en directo | Última hora de UEFA Nations League en vivo hoy
articles.summary: Los internacionales salen a ver el campo bien abrigados. Foto: Chema Rey/MARCA Valles, Laporte y Nico Williams son los descartes de España en Praga La
articles.body:
Última hora del República Checa - España en directo

Muuuuuuuuuy buenas tardeeeeeeeeeees. Y son buenas, porque vamos a ver a España . La Selección afronta el cierre del año con su contador de derrotas a cero. Con la segunda estrella en su camiseta. Y un mensaje de dominio mundial que pocas veces se ha visto en la historia del fútbol. Dos empates y catorce triunfos conforman la hoja de ruta de España en este ya histórico y memorable 2026. Hoy, en Chequia , toca mantener el nivel y volver a sacarle brillo a la estrella.

En la ventana pasada, la selección española dejó dos victorias cargadas de significado, las de Wembley y Split . En ambas se vio con el marcador en contra y con ambientes electrizados por la ventaja de los locales ante la campeona del mundo y de Europa . Y en los dos casos se elevó por encima de las dificultades y voló de vuelta a casa con la victoria. Esta noche no podrá contar con dos nombres importantes como Lamine Yamal y Mikel Oyarzabal , ausencias de peso en una selección que desde marzo de 2023 apenas conoce otra palabra que no sea éxito.

Enfrente aparece una República Checa que tiene una historia muy ligada al fútbol español. En su banquillo se sienta Santi Denia , campeón olímpico con España en París y uno de los técnicos con más influencia en la construcción de la generación que ha llevado a la selección a dominar el fútbol europeo. Entre 2010 y 2025 formó parte de la estructura de la Federación , acompañando el crecimiento de buena parte de los internacionales que ahora tendrá enfrente. Ningún seleccionador rival conoce tan bien a España como él.

Enseguida conocemos los onces, tenemos noticias desde Chequia y conectamos con nuestros enviados especiales en el estadio para que nos cuenten esas cositas que nosotros no vemos desde aquí. No esperamos más y arrrrrrrancamooooooooos.

articles.title: Inglaterra - Croacia en directo | Última hora de UEFA Nations League en vivo hoy
articles.summary: Los defensas Marc Guéhi y Ezri Konsa han causado baja en la selección inglesa para este partido por lesión. Tuchel ha convocado en su lugar a Dan Burn
articles.body:
Última hora del Inglaterra - Croacia en directo:

Muy buenas tardes a todos. Arrancamos con la narración en directo del partido Inglaterra - Croacia , correspondiente a la quinta jornada de la Liga de Naciones .

Inglaterra y Croacia están encuadradas en el el Grupo A3 junto a España y la República Checa . Los ingleses, que aún tiene opciones de clasificarse como primeros de grupo para cuartos de final de la competición, podría certificar hoy matemáticamente su pase simplemente sacando un empate. Para aspirar al primer puesto deberán ganar a la selección balcánica.

El partido tiene tintes de revancha para Croacia, que el pasado 3 de octubre perdió por un contundente 0-7 frente al Inglaterra, una derrota que fue calificada como humillante y que constituye la más abultada en la historia de la selección croata.

El partido arranca a las 20:45 horas en el Wembley y será arbitrado por el colegiado danés Morten Krogh . Estará respaldado desde el VAR por el alemán Bastian Dankert . Queda presentado el partido. Desde ya os vamos a ir contando todas las novedades que se produzcan en torno a este partido. Comenzamos.

articles.title: Zero question about the biggest key for USC against Indiana
articles.summary: The USC offensive line versus the Indiana defensive line stands out as the biggest position battle in Saturday's showdown
articles.body:
USC versus Indiana is a season-defining game for both teams. The defending champion Hoosiers might miss the College Football Playoff if they lose. USC definitely won't make the playoff if it falls short, and fresh criticism will greet embattled coach Lincoln Riley. In a very high-stakes game, the biggest and most central key is a natural point of interest. Our view on this topic is clear.

The USC offensive line versus the Indiana defensive line is by far the most important position-group battle on the field in Bloomington. Indiana's quarterback situation is a mess, and Indiana's special teams are shaky. Indiana's obvious strength, the core of the team and the reason the Hoosiers have lost only once this season despite some terrible offensive performances, is its defensive line. Many aspects of the 2026 Indiana team are noticeably worse than the 2025 national championship squad, but the defensive line isn't one of them. This is the heartbeat and backbone of the Hoosiers.

Mindful of how great USC looked when the offensive line thrived against Ohio State, and mindful of how bad USC looked when the offensive line no-showed at Wisconsin, it stands to reason that the way the Trojans ' offensive front performs will define how this Indiana game unfolds. Either USC scores 27 - which a sputtering Indiana offense will struggle to do - or USC scores just 10 or 13 points, giving Indiana more than enough margin for error on offense.

Many aspects of this game matter, but none are likely to matter more than the USC O-line against the Indiana D-line.

articles.title: The cost of failure at Man United keeps rising as compensation payouts mount
articles.summary: MANCHESTER, England (AP) — Manchester United has spent well in excess of $100 million to pay off failed coaches and soccer executives during more than a deca...
articles.body:
MANCHESTER, England (AP) — Manchester United has spent well in excess of $100 million to pay off failed coaches and soccer executives during more than a decade of onfield decline.

And that was before Michael Carrick became the seventh manager to be fired since club great Alex Ferguson retired in 2013. United is closing in on a deal to hire U.S. men's national team coach Mauricio Pochettino .

It is not yet known how much compensation Carrick will be due following his dismissal less than six months into a two-year contract. What is known is that failure at United can be a very lucrative business.

It cost 19.6 million pounds ($26 million) to relieve Jose Mourinho and his staff of their duties 11 months after he signed a long-term deal in 2018.

It was 10.4 million pounds ($13.76m) for Erik ten Hag and his staff three months after he signed a contract extension.

Ruben Amorim? United paid 11 million pounds ($14.55 million) to trigger his early release from Sporting Lisbon in November 2024 and 8.2 million pounds ($10.85 million) to pay off him and his staff 14 months later.

All this from a club that is swimming in debt and has implemented brutal cost-cutting measures to try to arrest its financial problems.

Last year minority owner Jim Ratcliffe warned that United was enduring unsustainable losses and under his watch the club has laid off hundreds of staff and sparked fan protests after hiking up ticket prices.

Despite that the British billionaire has overseen a slew of costly errors since buying an initial 25% stake in the club in 2024 and assuming control of its soccer operations.

It was under Ratcliffe that Ten Hag was given a new contract and then promptly fired. Amorim was his first coaching hire and that ended swiftly and at great expense.

Then there was Dan Ashworth's appointment as director of football. United paid a reported 2-3 million pounds ($2.65-4 million) to prise him away from Premier League rival Newcastle, while Ashworth also spent five months on gardening leave during negotiations.

He was out of the door less than six months later, with United's accounts revealing a cost of 4.1 million pounds ($5.4 million) for the whole episode, including compensation hire him.

That's a total of 33.7 million pounds ($44.56 million) under Ratcliffe's watch alone. And it could have been worse, with Amorim's appointment by AC Milan this year reducing the maximum compensation United was due to pay from a potential maximum figure of 16.7 million ($22.1 million).

However, such lavish spending on failed projects pre-dates Ratcliffe's investment.

United paid out 5.2 million pounds ($6.88 million) when David Moyes was fired 11 months into a six-year contract in 2014.

Louis van Gaal was fired two days after winning the FA Cup in 2016, prompting compensation of 8.4 million pounds ($11.11 million).

articles.title: 'It's just quite simply disgusting' - Gary Neville slams Manchester United's leadership over the way they handled Michael Carrick's sacking
articles.summary: Gary Neville has called Manchester United's handling of Michael Carrick's sacking "quite simply disgusting", hitting out at the board for meeting in Monaco a...
articles.body:
Carrick sacked after worst start in four decades

Carrick was relieved of his duties on Thursday morning after a dreadful start to the season left United 18th in the Premier League. They have won just one of their opening 10 league matches, their worst start to a campaign in four decades.

Co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe attended a senior Ineos staff meeting in Monaco, where Carrick's future is thought to have been discussed with director of football Jason Wilcox and chief executive Omar Berrada. United reached an agreement in principle with Pochettino on Wednesday, while Carrick was still taking training at Carrington.

Neville says United watched Carrick 'resign on the pitch'

Neville had already called the timing "classless" on the Stick to Football podcast before the announcement, and he went further once the decision was made. Speaking to Sky Sports, he said: "I think after the Bournemouth game I said at the time that Manchester United effectively watched Michael Carrick resign on the pitch at the end of the game with that lap around, that wave goodbye. I think he was expecting it to come at that point and they were indecisive."

He continued: "They obviously felt that they might be able to get to the international break and there could be some sort of pick-up in results, but it's been a difficult two weeks. Indecision, lack of authority, just basically really poor leadership."

Neville saved his strongest criticism for the decision-makers being away from Manchester as the process played out. "In the last 24-48 hours it's been spectacularly bad to be in Monaco as an executive and an owner whilst your manager, who's a club legend, is taking training on the pitch and simultaneously approaching the US Soccer Federation to approach Mauricio Pochettino," he added.

"It's just quite simply disgusting. That falls well below the standard of what you would expect in any other business, in any other industry. It would be constructive dismissal and you'd be getting sued. The optics of being in Monaco whilst the team, the staff, the people who are running the club on a day-to-day basis are in Manchester, it's just not good and it reflects badly on the leadership. I don't think anybody comes out of this well at all."

Pochettino is not expected to take charge at Old Trafford until next week.

He will first lead the United States in their CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final against Haiti, with the first leg in Miami on Saturday. The return game in Cincinnati takes place next Tuesday night, finishing in the early hours of Wednesday UK time.
